# Session state (survives context compaction)

Updated: 2026-11-17. Target: **samsung-j7elte**, SM-J700M, Nura (pmOS) 3.10.108.

## Device access
- USB net: host `172.16.42.2/24`, device `172.16.42.1`; SSH `user@172.16.42.1` (password `nura`).
- Host tools: `SSH_ASKPASS=/tmp/ap.sh` (echoes `nura`), `setsid -w ssh ...`.
- Reboot: `echo 1 > /proc/sys/kernel/sysrq; echo b > /proc/sysrq-trigger` (**sync first** — sysrq-b does not sync; unsynced writes were lost once).
- Recovery: TWRP = Power 20 s, then Vol Up+Home+Power; then
  `adb push boot.img /data/ && adb shell 'dd if=/data/boot.img of=/dev/block/mmcblk0p10 bs=512 conv=fsync; sync; reboot'`.
  Known-good boot image: `/tmp/bindboot.img` (host).

- Kernel: our build of `LineageOS/android_kernel_samsung_universal7580@2a746c1b`

  Rebuild: `code/kernel/build.sh` (GCC 16.2, `KCFLAGS=-Wno-error`), then

content.text:
## 22. Front sensor fails identically: not a rear-camera hardware fault

`j7elte-cam -f` originally looked for `31s/31c`, which this driver does not
register; the front S5K5E3 shares the single 3AA/ISP group (`30s/30c/i0s/scp`)
and differs only in the sensor node (`ss1`) and sensor id. Patched the tool to
do that; the pipeline then runs for the front sensor:

```
[@][1][SEN:D] fimc_is_sensor_s_input(17, 0):0
[TS:...] [SENS][00|00][17|05] [OpenSensor] is called. I2c Ch:1
[TS:...][ERROR]Sensor I2C doesn't work. I2C ch(1),Addr:0x20 -
                         Interrupt Status Register: 0x5100
[TS:...][ERROR][send] ... m_I2CNackErrCount(1)
```

Different sensor (S5K5E3), different ISP I2C channel (1) and different address
(0x20) - **identical NACK**. So the rear camera module is not faulty; the
shared ISP firmware -> sensor I2C path fails for both cameras. That also
matches the DEAD actuator/flash ids the firmware reports (`Actuator 0,
Flash 5` for the front, vs `13/11` for the rear) being read from the same
non-working bus.

Consequence for the remaining work: debug the ISP I2C block itself (clock
gate / bus init inside FIMC-IS), not the sensor, the mux or the rails.

## 23. Firmware RE: the missing HIC_ISP_I2C_CONTROL path

The ISP firmware (`fimc_is_fw2_3l2.bin`, 2.8 MB, raw ARM image) contains its
own I2C stack:

```
[ISP_I2C_WaitForBusReady][ch %d] timeout (ErrCnt:%d)
[I2CHAL_CalcInit] g_I2C_SCLK is NULL.
[EC__] I2C Clock : Host = %d --> g_I2C_SCLK = %d (Fixed:%s)
Sensor I2C doesn't work. I2C ch(%d),Addr:0x%02x - Interrupt Status Register: 0x%X
HIC_SET_ISP_I2C_CONTROL
```

`HIC_SET_ISP_I2C_CONTROL` names the host-interface command that configures
that I2C block.  The kernel enum has it
(`include/fimc-is-cmd.h: HIC_ISP_I2C_CONTROL`), **but no driver code sends or
handles it** - the only I2C-related HIC in the message switch is
`HIC_I2C_CONTROL_LOCK` (`fimc-is-interface.c:1073` handles it, `:3418` sends
it).  So the firmware's ISP I2C block is never configured by the host, which
matches the NACK on an otherwise fully powered, muxed, open pipeline, and it
matches the firmware complaining after programming `g_I2C_SCLK = 26 MHz`
itself.

Next concrete step: implement the host side of `HIC_ISP_I2C_CONTROL` (reply to
the request / send the configuration the stock host sends - parameters can be
recovered by disassembling the surrounding code of that string in the firmware,
or the stock HAL's callers), or find the V4L2 control in the vendor HAL that
triggers it.

#ifndef FIMC_IS_CMD_H
#define FIMC_IS_CMD_H

#include "fimc-is-config.h"

#define IS_COMMAND_VER 132 /* IS COMMAND VERSION 1.32 */

enum is_cmd {
	/* HOST -> IS */
	HIC_PREVIEW_STILL = 0x1,
	HIC_PREVIEW_VIDEO,
	HIC_CAPTURE_STILL,
	HIC_CAPTURE_VIDEO,
	HIC_PROCESS_START,
	HIC_PROCESS_STOP,
	HIC_STREAM_ON /* 7 */,
	HIC_STREAM_OFF /* 8 */,
	HIC_SHOT,
	HIC_GET_STATIC_METADATA /* 10 */,
	HIC_SET_CAM_CONTROL,
	HIC_GET_CAM_CONTROL,
	HIC_SET_PARAMETER /* 13 */,
	HIC_GET_PARAMETER,
	HIC_SET_A5_MAP /* 15 */,
	HIC_SET_A5_UNMAP /* 16 */,
	HIC_FAULT,
	/* SENSOR PART*/
	HIC_OPEN_SENSOR,
	HIC_CLOSE_SENSOR,
	HIC_SIMMIAN_INIT /* 20 */,
	HIC_SIMMIAN_WRITE,
	HIC_SIMMIAN_READ,
	HIC_POWER_DOWN,
	HIC_GET_SET_FILE_ADDR,
	HIC_LOAD_SET_FILE,
	HIC_MSG_CONFIG,
	HIC_MSG_TEST,
	HIC_ISP_I2C_CONTROL,
	HIC_CALIBRATE_ACTUATOR,
	HIC_GET_IP_STATUS /* 30 */,
	HIC_I2C_CONTROL_LOCK,
#if (SUPPORTED_IS_CMD_VER >= 132)
	HIC_SYSTEM_CONTROL,
	HIC_SENSOR_MODE_CHANGE,
#elif (SUPPORTED_IS_CMD_VER >= 131)
	HIC_SENSOR_MODE_CHANGE,
#endif
	HIC_ADJUST_SET_FILE,
	HIC_CHECK_A5_TASK_CPU_USAGE,
	HIC_COMMAND_END,

	/* IS -> HOST */
	IHC_GET_SENSOR_NUMBER = 0x1000,
	/* Parameter1 : Address of space to copy a setfile */
	/* Parameter2 : Space szie */
	IHC_SET_SHOT_MARK,
	/* PARAM1 : a frame number */
	/* PARAM2 : confidence level(smile 0~100) */
	/* PARMA3 : confidence level(blink 0~100) */
	IHC_SET_FACE_MARK,
	/* PARAM1 : coordinate count */
	/* PARAM2 : coordinate buffer address */
	IHC_FRAME_DONE,
	/* PARAM1 : frame start number */
	/* PARAM2 : frame count */
	IHC_AA_DONE,
	IHC_NOT_READY,
	IHC_FLASH_READY,
#if (SUPPORTED_IS_CMD_VER >= 131)
	IHC_REPORT_ERR,
#endif
	IHC_COMMAND_END
};

Important: index 0 = UNKNOWN, index 1 = HIC_PREVIEW_STILL... so index == command id. Index 28 = HIC_SET_ISP_I2C_CONTROL. But kernel enum HIC_ISP_I2C_CONTROL = 27, and string in firmeware at index 27 is HIC_MSG_TEST, index 28 HIC_SET_ISP... Hmm! Wait docs said index distance matches: HIC_OPEN_SENSOR 17? But here HIC_OPEN_SENSOR is at index 18, HIC_FAULT 17. Kernel enum: HIC_FAULT=17, HIC_OPEN_SENSOR=18. Let's count: 1 PREVIEW_STILL ... HIC_FAULT = 17, HIC_OPEN_SENSOR=18. Then HIC_ISP_I2C_CONTROL = 27, HIC_CALIBRATE_ACTUATOR=28.

Firmware table: index 27 = HIC_MSG_TEST; 28 = HIC_SET_ISP_I2C_CONTROL; 29 = HIC_CALIBRATE_ACTUATOR. So firmware table appears shifted by +1 for everything after index 18? Check index 18=HIC_OPEN_SENSOR matches kernel 18. 19 CLOSE_SENSOR matches. 20 SIMMIAN_INIT matches, 21 WRITE, 22 READ, 23 POWER_DOWN, 24 GET_SET_FILE_ADDR, 25 LOAD_SET_FILE, 26 MSG_CONFIG, 27 MSG_TEST, 28 SET_ISP_I2C_CONTROL, 29 CALIBRATE_ACTUATOR, 30 GET_IP_STATUS.

Yes! I mis-assigned earlier. So HIC_ISP_I2C_CONTROL = 28, not 27. >>> nodes has an disadvantage that we need dummy I2C bus controller driver,
>>> at least this is how I have written the driver for Exynos4x12. In some
>>> version of it I had sensor nodes put in a isp-i2c fimc-is sub-node, but
>>> then there was an issue that this was not a fully specified I2C bus
>>> controller node.
>>>
>>> You can refer to my exynos4 fimc-is patch series for details on how this
>>> is now implemented.
>>>
>>> Handling the image sensor in a standard way, as regular I2C client
>>> devices
>>> has an advantage that we can put pinctrl properties in relevant device
>>> nodes,
>>> where available, which more closely describes the hardware structure.
>>>
>>> I'm not really sure in 100% if all this complication is required. It
>>> would
>>> allow to use same DT blob for different Imaging Subsystem SW
>>> architecture.
>>> For example some parts of functionality handled currently by FIMC-IS (ARM
>>> Cortex-A5) could be moved to host CPU, without any change in the device
>>> tree structure. The kernel could decide e.g. if it uses image sensor
>>> driver
>>> implemented in the ISP firmware, or a driver run on the host CPU.
>>>
>>> What do you think ?
>>
>>
>> I have seen your Exynos4 FIMC-IS patchset and you have made a dummy
>> I2C sensor driver there.
>> That mode would work fine in Exynos4 since the sensor and ISP will be used
>> by the same media controller pipeline. So the ISP component in the
>> pipeline
>> will ensure that the HW is initialized and sensor is working.
>>
>> But in Exynos5, we are using sensor in pipeline0 and ISP in pipeline1.
>> So there is a possibility of using sensor subdev independently
>> without using pipeline1 ISP components.
>>
>> So with the driver I sent, the pipeline0 can still work like this -->
>>
>> ISP sensor --->  MIPI-CSIS --->  FIMC-LITE --->  Memory
>>
>> This cannot be done if a dummy I2C driver is made for ISP sensor.
>
>
> Why not ? I'm not sure what the problem is here.
>
> I realize that describing image sensors in DT as standard I2C slave devices
> is not helpful with current firmware architecture. It adds some unnecessary
> complication, OTOH it could simplify the sensors registration and media
> graph
> initialization code, by unifying it for the firmware based ISP specific
> sensors and the external ones with a built-in ISP. Also we could avoid
> having
> the bindings defined by current architecture of the driver.
>
> Nevertheless, coming back to your question, the I2C controller driver would
> be in same module as the FIMC-IS driver. From user space perspective nothing
> changes when you add I2C bus driver and register the sensor in a standard
> way.
> What exactly couldn't be done in the kernel ?
Only issue is with the context sharing.
Right now you can see that the fimc-is context is shared between all
the subdevs.
As all of them are part of the same driver, it is possible.
If sensor is made as an independent i2c device, a separate probe will
be called for it.
For ISP sensor subdev to work independently, it needs to call the
fimc_is_pipeline_* calls
for FW initialization and other configurations for which it needs the
fimc-is main context.

Now there is a workaround here by calling a get_context() macro in
sensor's probe
to get the fimc-is context. This will cause the same context to be
shared and updated by
2 drivers though both are part of fimc-is.
Is this acceptable? Or am I missing some other simple solution of implementing
it in a better way?

Regards
Arun

sources.title: Exynos5 FIMC-IS driver  [LWN.net]
sources.snippet:
But in case of Exynos5, the fimc-capture IP is removed and instead a more 
powerful fimc-is takes the role of giving scaled image output via DMA.
FIMC-IS internally has two scalers for this in addition to other
post-processing components like dynamic range compression,
optical distortion correction, digital image stabilization, 3D noise reduction
and face detection.

FIMC-IS also has capability to directly control certain sensors and the
sensors compatible with the fimc-is will be termed as fimc-is sensors.
This patchset adds support for two such fimc-is sensors - s5k4e5 and s5k6a3.
These sensors are controlled exclusively by the fimc-is firmware.
They provide only SRGB unscaled output which will reach fimc-is
via mipi-csis and fimc-lite. The color space conversion, scaling and all other
post processing will be then done by the fimc-is IP components.

The fimc-is driver operates in the following manner:
The sensor subdevice created by this driver will be used by the exynos5
media-device's pipeline0 which connects it with mipi-csis and fimc-lite.

|fimc-is-sensor|--->|mipi-csis|--->|fimc-lite|--->|Memory|

The output bayer image dumped by the fimc-lite subdev into memory is fed
into the ISP subdev of fimc-is driver. For that the pipeline1 of exynos5
media-device will look like this:

|Memory|--->|fimc-is-isp|--->|fimc-is-scaler-codec|--->|fimc-is-scaler-preview|

The isp subdev accepts bayer input buffer at its OUTPUT_MPLANE. It will
do a set of post processing operations and passes it on-the-fly to the
scalers. The two scalers can give two different scaled outputs which can
be used for recording and preview simultaneously. Both scaler-codec and
scaler-preview dumps DMA data out through its CAPTURE_MPLANE.

This first RFC contains the basic version of the driver which accepts
bayer input data and provides 2 different scaled outputs with most of
the post processing blocks disabled.

This has to be applied on exynos5 media device patchset posted by
Shaik Ameer Basha [1] and its based on media-tree v3.9.

That's relevant: the ISP I2C is a separate I2C adapter driven by the *host*, not firmware, in mainline. In vendor firmware, the ISP I2C block is driven by firmware. This project demonstrates the implementation of I2C communication using the I2C1 peripheral on an STM32 microcontroller. The program initializes I2C1, configures GPIO pins for I2C communication, and performs basic read and write operations to a slave device over the I2C bus.

The actual I2C transaction is inside 0xcc0e/0xcc1e/0xcc2a, which thunk to 0x4xxx. The NACK is detected where? `func_0x0000cc0e` returns 0 on failure; logs "I2CHAL_IntrSendStart fail". The actual status register 0x5100 printed in earlier log comes from `func_0x0000cc36` (read +0x20 & 0xffff) in the open-sensor path.

We need to know what bits 0x4000/0x1000 mean. Possibly:
- bit 8 (0x100): TX interrupt (transfer started)
- bit 12 (0x1000): NACK
- bit 14 (0x4000): ??? 

If bit 12 is NACK, then indeed the sensor is not ACKing. Why? Bus lines or slave address.

Wait: the error printed "Addr:0x5a". The sensor's 7-bit address 0x2d (0x5a<<1). If the firmware sends to 0x5a and no ACK, maybe the sensor is held in reset? But the sensor was powered and reset released; the kernel read its ID? Hmm, does anything verify the sensor ID? The pipeline got as far as OpenSensor, so the sensor is powered. If the sensor's I2C lines aren't connected (mux wrong), no ACK.

Let's inspect the pinmux more concretely. GPF0 pins:
- gpf0-0, gpf0-1 → fimc_is_i2c0 (function 2)
- gpf0-2, gpf0-3 → fimc_is_i2c1 (function 2)

Function 2 on GPF0 in Exynos 7580 likely maps to "I2C0_ISP" / "I2C1_ISP" (the ISP's I2C controllers). That seems right.

But maybe these pins also connect to the AP's I2C controllers (function 3?) and the *kernel* uses them for the sensor via i2c-gpio? The EEPROM uses gpc2 (rear) and gpf0 (front) as GPIO bit-bang. Hmm, front EEPROM uses gpf0-2/3, same pins as front sensor I2C1! The kernel bit-bangs EEPROM on these pins during firmware load (fimc_is_rear_eeprom...)? Actually the EEPROM "fimc_is_eeprom_i2c@10" on i2c bus? It has sda/scl pin names for gpio i2c. The kernel reads cal data via GPIO I2C, toggling pinmux to GPIO. After that, the pinctrl state for sensor on sets function 2. Fine.

Another thought: The ISP I2C may need the sensor's *MCLK* running (it is), and the sensor needs a small delay after power before ACK. But both sensors identical failure and firmware worked in stock — likely our kernel leaves something unconfigured, e.g., the ISP I2C controller's clock gate.

Let's inspect the clock gate registers from the log: EN_SCLK_ISP=0xFFF. This might include bit for I2C. If the ISP I2C input clock is off, transfers would fail with bus timeout (bit 0x1000?) and NACK-like status.

Look at the SoC clock driver: does the ISP I2C have a gate? Search the 7580 clock driver for "i2c_isp" or "sclk_i2c".

#!/bin/sh
# Build linux-samsung-j7elte (3.10.108) for j7elte and produce an Android boot.img
# that S-Boot accepts.  Verified on 2026-11-17: Image builds with GCC 16,
# boots on the phone; do NOT touch the dt.img (see docs section 16).
set -eu
WORK=${WORK:-/run/media/asdf/db69437b-ed35-414a-8bd1-bade16b06830/j7k}
SHA=2a746c1bc1a41eae05988c153f527c8a5dc72d07
SRC=$WORK/android_kernel_samsung_universal7580-$SHA
PMD=$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/../.." && pwd)/code/pmaports/device/archived/linux-samsung-j7elte

[ -d "$SRC" ] || {
	mkdir -p "$WORK" && cd "$WORK"
	curl -sL -o k.tar.gz "https://codeload.github.com/LineageOS/android_kernel_samsung_universal7580/tar.gz/$SHA"
	tar xzf k.tar.gz
}

cd "$SRC"
cp "$PMD/config-samsung-j7elte.aarch64" .config
for p in "$PMD"/*.patch; do
	patch -p1 -N -r - < "$p" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
done
yes "" | make ARCH=arm64 CROSS_COMPILE=aarch64-linux-gnu- oldconfig >/dev/null

make ARCH=arm64 CROSS_COMPILE=aarch64-linux-gnu- KCFLAGS="-Wno-error" -j2 Image
ls -l arch/arm64/boot/Image

# Boot image: reuse the reference ramdisk/cmdline and the STOCK dt.img.
# Replacing the DTB payloads inside the DTBH container makes S-Boot hang, and
# a rebuilt DTB is not needed (same source content), so keep /tmp/bimg/dt.img.
if [ -f /tmp/bimg/dt.img ]; then
	python3 /tmp/mkboot.py arch/arm64/boot/Image /tmp/bimg/ramdisk-new.gz \
		/tmp/bimg/dt.img /tmp/kernel-boot.img "$(cat /tmp/bimg/cmdline)"
	echo "boot image: /tmp/kernel-boot.img"
fi
cmdline
dt.img
kernel
ramdisk-new.gz
ramdisk.gz

The front tool fails because i0s is in "stream off state, can NOT qbuf". Why? The tool's sequence sets END_OF_STREAM control on a3s (30s) before S_INPUT. For front, the a3s is 30s too. `fimc_is_ischain_open_wrap` probably only opens the group for the *rear* sensor? Or the stream off state is because S_INPUT on i0s with front sensor id failed silently and closed.

Maybe the second leader S_INPUT (i0s) succeeded but the group state is off because the sensor is front and the driver's `fimc_is_ischain_init` failed (returned EINVAL) but the tool ignores? No, it checks.

This is a tool/kernel path issue, not worth chasing now.

Let's instead test whether the *rear module* is dead by swapping to the front sensor's channel? Can't.

Better: instrument the kernel to add an I2C bit-bang test on gpf0-0/1 with rails on at the exact moment, using the existing gpio driver. We can write a *tiny userspace* test that:
1. Powers the rear sensor via the same sysfs? Not possible.
2. But we can trigger power-on via the camera S_INPUT, then before firmware boot, pause? Our ischain.c code runs at power-on; we could add a *long delay* (e.g., 30s) in the kernel before firmware boot, during which rails/reset/MCLK are on and pins are GPIO? If we add an mdelay(30000), we can then from userspace export gpf0 pins, bit-bang I2C, and test ACK. That's a debugging kernel, but doable. However, we already have a strong suspicion the module works (it's stock hardware).

Alternative: after the failed open, the sensor is powered off. But we can keep it powered by writing a small kernel hack to not power off? Too much.

Let's revisit the firmware I2C error. Maybe the **ISP I2C controller is not the sensor bus** because function 2 is actually the AP I2C0 controller. The EEPROM front pinfunc_off = 2 means "switch back to the sensor's function", which could be the *AP I2C* that the kernel uses to talk to the front EEPROM? Wait, no: the EEPROM's pinfunc_off = 2 is used when turning *off* the EEPROM bit-bang, restoring function 2, which is the function used by the **sensor** (not EEPROM). So function 2 is the sensor's I2C bus. It must be the ISP I2C (firmware-driven) since the kernel never talks to the sensor. Unless the kernel's sensor driver *does* talk to the sensor on an AP I2C controller for ID/init.

Does the 3l2 module probe read the sensor ID over I2C? Search for i2c in 3l2 module (not the EEPROM file). The 3l2 is a platform device; pdata->gpio_cfg only. No i2c_transfer in 3l2.c (grep earlier didn't show). So the kernel doesn't talk to the sensor. Therefore function 2 must be the ISP I2C.

OK.

Maybe the sensor requires the **MCLK frequency to be 24MHz** and our MCLK is 26MHz or off. Let's verify the MCLK rate from the clock driver: `fimc_is_sensor_mclk_on` calls the platform `mclk_on` which likely sets `sclk_isp_sensor0` rate. Check fimc-is-dt.c mclk functions and DT clock names.

+
+fimc-is node
+------------
+
+Required properties:
+
+- compatible        : should contain "samsung,exynos5250-fimc-is"
+- reg               : physical base address and size of the memory mapped
+                      registers
+- interrupts        : interrupt-specifier for the fimc-is interrupt
+- clocks            : list of clock specifiers, corresponding to entries in
+                      clock-names property
+- clock-names       : must contain "isp", "mcu_isp", "isp_div0", "isp_div1",
+                      "isp_divmpwm", "mcu_isp_div0", "mcu_isp_div1" entries,
+                      matching entries in the clocks property
+- samsung,pmu       : phandle to the Power Management Unit (PMU) node
+
+i2c-isp (ISP I2C bus controller) nodes
+--------------------------------------
+The i2c-isp nodes should be children of the fimc-is node.
+
+Required properties:
+
+- compatible   : must contain "samsung,exynos4212-i2c-isp" for Exynos4212,
+                 Exynos4412 and Exynos5250 SoCs
+- reg          : physical base address and length of the registers set
+- clocks       : should contain gate clock specifier for this controller
+- clock-names  : should contain "i2c_isp" for the gate clock
+- pinctrl-0    : phandle of the pinctrl node for the i2c isp
+- pinctrl-names : must contain "default"
+
+ranges, #address-cells, and #size-cells should be present as appropriate.
+
+Device tree nodes of the image sensors controlled directly by the FIMC-IS
+firmware must be child nodes of their corresponding ISP I2C bus controller 
node.

+interfaces bindings, defined in video-interfaces.txt.

+       };

content.thinking:
No.

Let's use the firmware to read the I2C status bits semantics by examining the **ISP I2C driver in old Samsung firmware source leaks**? Not available.

Alternative: Search the firmware for the strings around the status print and the code path that decides NACK. The print at 0x35694 reads status via cc36 (+0x20 & 0xffff). The decision path: `func_0xcc36` returns status; then the queue marks failure based on `func_0xcc0e`? The status print happens unconditionally on the error path, but what determined the error? At 0x3568a:
```
bl 0xccb8(ch,0)   ; clear queue?
bl 0xcc36(ch)     ; read status
log "Sensor I2C doesn't work ... status"
```
This is the error path after a failed read/write. The failure condition was evaluated before (func_0xcc0a etc.). The status may just be diagnostic. The actual NACK detection could be based on the RX data (0xff) or an ACK flag.

What if the sensor *is* ACKing but the firmware reads 0xFF data and considers it a failure? The log says "Sensor I2C doesn't work" based on status bits though.

Look at `func_0x45de` wait bus ready: it polls +0x04 bit 0x20 (bus busy?) for 9999 iterations; if it times out, logs "[ISP_I2C_WaitForBusReady] timeout". We do not see that log, so the bus became ready.

Then `func_0x468c(ch,1)` starts a write; writes data; then completion. The status 0x5100 after failure. If the sensor ACKed, the status would be different.

Let's determine bit meaning from hardware behavior: For an I2C write to a non-existent address, the controller sets NACK interrupt. The status likely has bit 0x4000 = NACK. For a successful write, status might be 0x0100 (transfer complete). 0x5100 has 0x100 (done) + 0x1000 + 0x4000. Maybe 0x1000 = "no ACK on address", 0x4000 = "no ACK on data". content.thinking:
The Android 6 Samsung HAL source for Exynos 7580 likely lives in a device-specific repo not AOSP. But the binary is available; we can RE it.

Maybe the crucial insight is simpler: the HAL's camera *open* does not rely on firmware I2C at all for the sensor; it calls a **V4L2 control to read the sensor ID** that uses the **AP I2C** and initializes the sensor. Our tool doesn't. But the firmware OpenSensor does I2C for its own initialization, so the sensor must ACK anyway.

Wait, the firmware's I2C **doesn't necessarily talk to the sensor directly**; maybe it talks to the *actuator* or *EEPROM* at address 0x5A? No, 0x5A is the sensor.

Let's check the stock HAL's V4L2 control IDs used right after `s_input`. We can find them in the binary by disassembling around the `exynos_v4l2_s_input` PLT call. Let's import libexynoscamera into Ghidra and find xrefs to the imported function. Ghidra will create thunks. Then look at the calling function and the immediate control IDs passed to `exynos_v4l2_s_ctrl`.

Let's do Ghidra headless on libexynoscamera.so (ARM 32). Extract it from system.raw first (we have /tmp/exynoscam.so identical). Use exynoscam.so.

Script: find all references to `exynos_v4l2_s_input` (external symbol), then decompile containing function(s). Also find calls to `exynos_v4l2_s_ctrl` within those functions and print the arguments (control IDs) nearby via disassembly.

Simpler: use capstone to find BL to PLT entries. Need PLT addresses from the ELF. `readelf -r` gives relocations for exynos_v4l2_s_input. Use `objdump -d` with symbols? The .so has dynamic symbols; aarch32 objdump (host objdump supports ARM? earlier host objdump said UNKNOWN for aarch64; for ARM32 maybe supported? Use arm-linux-gnueabi-objdump? Check installed cross tools. We have aarch64 only? `which arm-linux-gnueabihf-objdump`.)

Let's check and disassemble.

content.thinking:
The names are generic. We need the high-level `ExynosCamera::start` function. Rather than chase symbols, look at the HAL's **log strings** around "startSensor" or "m_setInput" and find the function addresses via string xrefs. The stock HAL likely logs "DEBUG(%s):..." with function names; strings include "startSensor" etc.

Search strings in exynoscam.so for likely sequence names: "startPreview", "startSensor", "setInput", "sensor open", "create". Then xref the string and find code. Ghidra can list defined strings and references.

But what do we want to learn? The exact V4L2 control sequence. We can compare with our tool. Perhaps the HAL calls `setControl` on the **sensor node** with `V4L2_CID_IS_S_SENSOR_MODE`/`SENSOR_MODE_CHANGE` etc. But our firmware OpenSensor happens during `fimc_is_ischain_init` triggered by S_INPUT; the sensor is opened then. Missing controls after that wouldn't fix OpenSensor.

Unless the HAL performs a **sensor power-up/identity read** before S_INPUT that makes the sensor ready. Let's find the HAL's *sensor init* sequence: `ExynosCamera::create()` calls `exynos_v4l2_s_input` early (we saw in old source). The newer HAL's `m_startSensor` might:
1. open sensor video node
2. `setInput` (S_INPUT)
3. `s_ctrl(V4L2_CID_IS_END_OF_STREAM, 1)`
4. `s_ctrl(V4L2_CID_IS_S_SENSOR_MODE, ...)`
5. `s_ctrl(V4L2_CID_IS_S_PARAM, ...)`

Our tool does END_OF_STREAM on 30s before S_INPUT. Maybe the order matters: stock does S_INPUT first, then END_OF_STREAM. Let's check our tool: it sets HAL version and END_OF_STREAM on a3s, then S_INPUT on a3s. If END_OF_STREAM opens the ischain with a **default sensor position** and the following S_INPUT with front/rear causes a close/reopen, that could matter. 1. real user id(ruid) ：真实用户 ID。对于一个进程来说，真实用户 ID 就是启动该进程的用户的用户 ID。它定义了该进程可以访问哪些文件。
2. effective user id(euid) ：有效用户 ID。通常与真实用户 ID 相同，但有时会更改以使非特权用户能够访问只能由特权用户（如 root）访问的文件。
3. saved user id(suid) ：当一个进程以提升的权限（通常是 root）运行时，需要执行一些非特权工作时，可以通过暂时切换到非特权账户来实现。
在执行特权不足的工作时，有效的用户ID（UID）会被更改为较低的特权值，并将有效用户ID（EUID）保存为保存的用户ID（SUID），以便在任务完成后切换回特权账户。
如果您查看 /usr/bin/passwd 文件的权限：
代码语言： javascript
复制
-rwsr-xr-x 1 root root 59640 Mar 23  2019 /usr/bin/passwd
所以，如果非 root 用户运行此文件，进程的有效用户ID将为“0”，即 root，而用户 ID 将保持与原始用户相同。一个进程是否能操作某个文件，取决于进程的 euid 是否拥有这个文件的相应权限，而不是 ruid 。在具体一点，如果想要让进程拥有 root 用户的权限，只需要将 euid 设置为 0 （root 的 id）。
所以，sudo 本质上是一个拥有者为 root 且拥有 s 权限的可执行文件。

1. common : 包含与 sudo-rs 项目的一些通用功能相关的代码。
2. cutils : 包含 C 语言实用程序和函数的 Rust 实现。
3. defaults : 包含处理默认配置和设置的代码。
4. exec : 包含执行命令和进程管理相关的代码。
5. log : 包含日志记录功能的实现。
6. pam : 包含与 PAM (Pluggable Authentication Modules) 相关的代码，用于身份验证和会话管理。
7. su : 包含实现 su 命令功能的代码。
8. sudo : 包含实现 sudo 命令功能的代码。
9. sudoers : 包含解析和处理 sudoers 文件的代码。
10. system : 包含系统相关的实用程序和功能。
11. visudo : 包含 visudo 命令的实现，用于编辑 sudoers 文件。
12. lib.rs : 这是 Rust 项目的入口文件，通常用于模块声明和项目的总体组织。
13. macros.rs : 包含项目中使用的宏定义。

DESCRIPTION ¶

sudo allows a user that is permitted to do so to execute a command as another user (for example root ). Permissions are specified by a security policy specified in /etc/sudoers (see sudoers(5) ).
Sudo-rs is a safety oriented and memory safe re-implementation of the original sudo implementation by Todd Miller.
When a command is run, a session record is stored for that specific session allowing users to run additional commands without having to re-authenticate. The timeout for session records can be specified in the policy.
Some care is taken to pass signals received by sudo-rs to the child process, even if that process runs in its own pseudo terminal.

...

See sudoers(5) for more information.

* SUDO(8) | sudo-rs | SUDO(8)

NAME

sudo , sudoedit - execute a command as another user

SYNOPSIS

sudo -h | -K | -k | -V
sudo [ -u user ] [ -g group ] [ -D directory ] [ -BbknS ] [ -i | -s ] [ VAR=value ] [< command >]

sudo -e [ -BknS ] [ -u user ] [ -g group ] file ...
sudoedit [ -BknS ] [ -u user ] [ -g group ] file ...

DESCRIPTION

sudo allows a user that is permitted to do so to execute a command as another user (for example root ). Permissions are specified by a security policy specified in /etc/sudoers (see sudoers(5)).
Sudo-rs is a safety oriented and memory safe re-implementation of the original sudo implementation by Todd Miller.
When a command is run, a session record is stored for that specific session allowing users to run additional commands without having to re-authenticate. The timeout for session records can be specified in the policy.
Some care is taken to pass signals received by sudo-rs to the child process, even if that process runs in its own pseudo terminal.

sources.title: sudo-rs: Install the Memory-Safe sudo Replacement on Linux
sources.snippet:
Josphat Mutai Updated Apr 13, 2026 · 11 min read
Every Linux system has sudo. It’s the single binary standing between your unprivileged user account and full root access, which makes it one of the most security-critical programs on any server. The problem? Traditional sudo is written in C, and after 30+ years of patches, the codebase has accumulated its share of memory safety vulnerabilities.

...

* CVE-2019-14287 : User ID -1 was mishandled, letting a restricted user run commands as root. An integer handling bug that Rust’s type system would flag.
This doesn’t mean sudo-rs is vulnerability-free. Logic bugs can exist in any language. But the entire class of memory corruption vulnerabilities (the most dangerous kind, because they’re exploitable for arbitrary code execution) is eliminated by design.

 	unsigned long flags = 0;
 	struct pinctrl *pinctrl;

 	if ((buf == NULL) || kstrtouint(buf, 10, &value)) {

EOF

SectionDevice."Speaker" {
	Comment "Loudspeaker playback"

	EnableSequence [
		# route-ap-tx
		cset "name='S2801 Mixer En' 'On'"
		cset "name='S2801 CH1 Mixer En' 'On'"
		cset "name='S2801 CH2 Mixer En' 'Off'"
		cset "name='S2801 CH3 Mixer En' 'Off'"
		cset "name='S2801 CH4 Mixer En' 'Off'"
		cset "name='MonoMix Mode' 'Disable'"
		cset "name='Chargepump Mode' 'CLASS-G-A'"
		cset "name='DNC Max Gain' 24"
		# dev-codec-disable-analog-bypass
		cset "name='HPL Mixer ADCL Switch' off"
		cset "name='HPL Mixer ADCR Switch' off"
		cset "name='HPR Mixer ADCL Switch' off"
		cset "name='HPR Mixer ADCR Switch' off"
		cset "name='EP Mixer ADCL Switch' off"
		cset "name='EP Mixer ADCR Switch' off"
		cset "name='SPK Mixer ADCL Switch' off"
		cset "name='SPK Mixer ADCR Switch' off"
		# dev-speaker
		cset "name='HP HP On' off"
		cset "name='EP EP On' off"
		cset "name='SPK SPK On' on"
		# gain-media-speaker
		cset "name='S2801 MIX1_LVL' 0"
		cset "name='DAC Gain' 121"
		cset "name='Speaker Volume' 3"
	]

	DisableSequence [
		cset "name='SPK SPK On' off"
		cset "name='HP HP On' off"
		cset "name='EP EP On' off"
	]

	Value {
		PlaybackPriority 100
		PlaybackPCM "hw:${CardId},0"
		PlaybackChannels 2
		PlaybackRate 48000
	}
}

details.oldText:
# Session state (survives context compaction)

Updated: 2026-11-17. Target: **samsung-j7elte**, SM-J700M, Nura (pmOS) 3.10.108.

## Device access
- USB net: host `172.16.42.2/24`, device `172.16.42.1`; SSH `user@172.16.42.1` (password `nura`).
- Host tools: `SSH_ASKPASS=/tmp/ap.sh` (echoes `nura`), `setsid -w ssh ...`.
- Reboot: `echo 1 > /proc/sys/kernel/sysrq; echo b > /proc/sysrq-trigger` (**sync first** — sysrq-b does not sync; unsynced writes were lost once).
- Recovery: TWRP = Power 20 s, then Vol Up+Home+Power; then
  `adb push boot.img /data/ && adb shell 'dd if=/data/boot.img of=/dev/block/mmcblk0p10 bs=512 conv=fsync; sync; reboot'`.
  Known-good boot image: `/tmp/bindboot.img` (host).

## Working state on the phone
- Kernel: our build of `LineageOS/android_kernel_samsung_universal7580@2a746c1b`
  with patches `patches/camera/0001` (fw fallback), `0002` (FD optional),
  `0003` (ISP pin handover + rails re-enable at `fimc_is_ischain_power`).
  Rebuild: `code/kernel/build.sh` (GCC 16.2, `KCFLAGS=-Wno-error`), then
  `mkboot.py Image /tmp/bimg/ramdisk-new.gz /tmp/bimg/dt.img out.img "$(cat /tmp/bimg/cmdline)"`.
  **Never change the DTB payloads** — S-Boot hangs.
- `/usr` is bind-mounted from USERDATA in the initramfs (`patches/initramfs/0002`).
- Session: `rc-service xsession` -> `start-ui.sh` -> Xorg (with
  `LD_PRELOAD=/usr/local/lib/shadowfix.so`) -> `nura-shell` (phone UI).
- Firmware blobs in `/lib/firmware` (from stock J700MUBU2BRC2).
- `udev` v4l probe disabled: `/lib/udev/v4l_id.disabled` and
  `/etc/udev/rules.d/60-persistent-v4l.rules -> /dev/null`. **Re-apply after any
  apk transaction that reinstalls v4l-utils/udev.**

## Camera status (2026-11-18)
Green: sensor power sequencing, rails at voltage, reset high, MCLK 26 MHz
toggling at the pad, module EEPROM+cal CRC over I2C, signed firmware load,
ischain open, FD skipped.

Red: **both sensors are electrically silent on I2C.** A bit-bang master in
`fimc_is_ischain_power` (AP GPIOs gpf0-0/1 for ch0, gpf0-2/3 for ch1) scanned
0x08-0x77 at 100 kHz while the module was powered:
- rear: `VDD_CAM_SENSOR_A2P8 2.8 V, VDD_CAM_1P2 1.2 V, VDDIO 1.8 V,
  VDDAF 2.8 V`, reset gpe0-4 high, MCLK gate/rate/pad verified, full scan
  `none`;
- front: `VDD_VTCAM_A2P8 2.8 V, VDD_VTCAM_1P2 1.2 V, VDDIO_1.8V_VT 1.8 V`,
  `gpios_cam_en` toggling, reset gpe0-3 high, full scan finds **only the
  EEPROM at 0x10**, sensor at 0x20/0x5a never ACKs;
- rail power-cycle + 9-clock bus recovery + 100 ms reset delay changed
  nothing.
- The same NACK occurs with the **stock 3.10.61 vendor kernel** (boots the
  Nura rootfs), so this is not our kernel build.

Conclusion: the ISP-I2C/pin-mux theory is dead; the buses, EEPROMs, rails,
reset and MCLK are all verified good. The sensor dies themselves do not
respond, on both modules. Next step is hardware: reseat/measure the camera
connectors and the sensor core rails at the module.

### HIC_ISP_I2C_CONTROL (corrected)
Firmware command 28 is `HIC_SET_ISP_I2C_CONTROL` (index 28, not 27; kernel
enum agrees). Sending it with `param1=ch` is accepted but does not change the
NACK. Firmware uses fixed `g_I2C_SCLK=26 MHz`; I2CHAL computes
406 kHz/32 prescaler. Command 28's handler copies host data into a per-sensor
firmware buffer (AP->ISP I2C shadow), it does not initialise the ISP I2C block.

### Front flash + proximity (2026-11-18)
- Front flash (KTD2692, `front_torch_flash`) works. Patched for 5 levels
  (`patches/camera/0004`): laptop camera means 118.7/123.3/128.1/133.8/
  136.5/138.6 for off/L1..L5, p99 158->214. Confirms the front module is
  seated and powered.
- Proximity STK3013 on i2c-0 0x48 works: after

toggling at the pad, module EEPROM+cal CRC over I2C, signed firmware load,
ischain open, FD skipped.

details.newText:
# Audio routing configuration for the Samsung Galaxy J7 (j7elte).
#
# Installs an ALSA UCM2 profile for the ASoC sound card
# "Universal7580-I2S" (COD3022X codec + S2801X aux codec), derived from
# the stock ROM mixer graph.  Also installs the ROM's Android HAL jack
# configuration for reference.
#
# Control names were cross-checked against the Nura kernel sources; see
# parity/reports/audio-userspace.md.

pkgname=j7elte-audio-ucm
pkgver=0.1
pkgrel=0
pkgdesc="ALSA UCM2 profile and jack mixer data for Samsung Galaxy J7 (j7elte)"
url="https://postmarketos.org"
arch="aarch64"
# UCM routes are derived from the stock Samsung ROM mixer_paths.xml.
license="proprietary"
options="!check !archcheck"
depends="alsa-ucm-conf"

source="
	Universal7580-I2S.conf
	HiFi.conf
	VoiceCall.conf
	jack_alsa_mixer.json
"

build() {
	:
}

package() {
	install -Dm644 "$srcdir"/Universal7580-I2S.conf \
		"$pkgdir"/usr/share/alsa/ucm2/conf.d/Universal7580-I2S/Universal7580-I2S.conf
	install -Dm644 "$srcdir"/HiFi.conf \
		"$pkgdir"/usr/share/alsa/ucm2/j7elte/HiFi.conf
	install -Dm644 "$srcdir"/VoiceCall.conf \
		"$pkgdir"/usr/share/alsa/ucm2/j7elte/VoiceCall.conf
	install -Dm644 "$srcdir"/jack_alsa_mixer.json \
		"$pkgdir"/usr/share/j7elte-audio/jack_alsa_mixer.json
}

{"command":"cd /tmp && pactl set-default-source alsa_input.pci-0000_06_00.6.analog-stereo 2>&1 | tail -1; pactl set-source-volume alsa_input.pci-0000_06_00.6.analog-stereo 28% 2>&1 | tail -1; ( setsid ssh -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no user@172.16.42.1 'speaker-test -D hw:0,0 -t sine -f 440 -c 2 -l 10 >/dev/null 2>&1 & p=$!; sleep 1; amixer -c 0 cset "name=Speaker Volume" 15 >/dev/null 2>&1; wait $p' >/dev/null 2>&1 & ) ; sleep 1.2; SSH_ASKPASS=/tmp/ap.sh SSH_ASKPASS_REQUIRE=force timeout 10 setsid -w arecord -D pulse -f S16_LE -r 48000 -c 2 -d 6 /tmp/host_mic.wav 2>&1 | tail -1; python3 -c "
import wave,numpy as np
w=wave.open('/tmp/host_mic.wav');d=w.readframes(w.getnframes());sr=w.getframerate();w.close()
s=np.frombuffer(d,dtype='<i2').reshape(-1,2).mean(1).astype(float)
print('rms',round(np.sqrt((s*s).mean()),1),'peak',int(np.abs(s).max()))
x=s*np.hanning(len(s));X=np.abs(np.fft.rfft(x));f=np.fft.rfftfreq(len(s),1/sr)
print([(round(f[i],1),round(X[i])) for i in np.argsort(X)[-6:][::-1]])
for fr in (440,880,1000): j=np.argmin(abs(f-fr)); print(fr, round(X[j],1))
"","i":"Recording host mic during speaker test"}

DAPM switch names are expanded by ASoC as `"<widget> <control>"`
(`sound/soc/soc-dapm.c:655-660`, `snd_soc_cnew(..., prefix)`); e.g.
widget `SPK` + control `SPK On`
→ `SPK SPK On`.

### PCM device mapping

`soc_new_pcm(rtd, num)` is called with the DAI-link index
(`sound/soc/soc-core.c:1432`, `sound/soc/soc-pcm.c` `snd_pcm_new(..., num, ...)`),
so devices are assigned in link order:

| PCM | DAI link | Direction | Used by UCM |
|---|---|---|---|
| `hw:Card,0` | `universal7580-cod3022x` (`i2s0-pri`, `cod3022x-aif`) | playback + capture | HiFi |
| `hw:Card,1` | `universal7580-cod3022x-sec` (`i2s0-sec`) | playback | — |
| `hw:Card,2` | `cp` (`voice call`, `cod3022x-aif2`) | playback + capture | VoiceCall |
| `hw:Card,3` | `bt` (`dumy-aif2`) | playback + capture | — |
| `hw:Card,4` | `fm` (`FM audio`) | playback | — |
| `hw:Card,5` | `playback-eax0` | playback | — |
| `hw:Card,6` | `playback-eax1` | playback | — |

The card id is `Universal7580I2S` (ALSA keeps only alphanumerics when deriving
the id from the shortname, `sound/core/init.c` `copy_valid_id_string()`), while
the UCM directory uses the *driver* string with the dash
(`Universal7580-I2S`).  `alsaucm -c hw:0` is the safe invocation.

content.text:
### Vendor driver identity (stronger than name matching)

To rule out a source-level drift between 3.10.61 and 3.10.108, the codec's
static tables from the Nura source were compared against string constants in
`boot_out/vmlinux.elf`:

# HiFi use case for the Universal7580-I2S card (j7elte).
#
# Control names:
#   - un-prefixed        : COD3022X codec (sound/soc/codecs/cod3022x.c)
#   - "S2801 <name>"     : S2801X aux codec (sound/soc/codecs/s2801x.c);
#                          ASoC adds the "S2801" name_prefix from
#                          snd_soc_codec_conf in
#                          sound/soc/samsung/universal7580-cod3022x.c
#   - MXxx / XX On       : DAPM switches of the COD3022X codec
#
# Playback and capture PCM are DAI link 0 ("i2s0-pri", codec DAI
# "cod3022x-aif"), i.e. hw:${CardId},0 for both directions.

Syntax 3

SectionVerb {
	EnableSequence [
		# Stock ROM reset state (mixer_paths.xml top-level <ctl> set).
		cset "name='S2801 Mixer En' 'Off'"
		cset "name='S2801 SRC1 En' 'Off'"
		cset "name='S2801 SRC2 En' 'Off'"
		cset "name='S2801 SRC3 En' 'Off'"
		cset "name='S2801 CH1 Mixer En' 'Off'"
		cset "name='S2801 CH2 Mixer En' 'Off'"
		cset "name='S2801 CH3 Mixer En' 'Off'"
		cset "name='S2801 CH4 Mixer En' 'Off'"
		cset "name='S2801 RMIX1 En' 'Off'"
		cset "name='S2801 RMIX2 En' 'Off'"
		cset "name='S2801 CH3 Rec En' 'Off'"
		cset "name='S2801 CH1 DOUT Select' 'DMIX_OUT'"
		cset "name='S2801 CH2 DOUT Select' 'DMIX_OUT'"
		cset "name='S2801 CH3 DOUT Select' 'DMIX_OUT'"
		cset "name='MonoMix Mode' 'Disable'"
		cset "name='HP HP On' off"
		cset "name='EP EP On' off"
		cset "name='SPK SPK On' off"
		cset "name='Chargepump Mode' 'CLASS-G-A'"
		cset "name='DNC Max Gain' 24"
	]

	DisableSequence [
		cset "name='S2801 Mixer En' 'Off'"
		cset "name='S2801 SRC1 En' 'Off'"
		cset "name='S2801 SRC2 En' 'Off'"
		cset "name='S2801 SRC3 En' 'Off'"
		cset "name='S2801 CH1 Mixer En' 'Off'"
		cset "name='S2801 CH2 Mixer En' 'Off'"
		cset "name='S2801 CH3 Mixer En' 'Off'"
		cset "name='S2801 CH4 Mixer En' 'Off'"
		cset "name='S2801 RMIX1 En' 'Off'"
		cset "name='S2801 RMIX2 En' 'Off'"
		cset "name='S2801 CH3 Rec En' 'Off'"
		cset "name='HP HP On' off"
		cset "name='EP EP On' off"
		cset "name='SPK SPK On' off"
	]
}

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- playback

SectionDevice."Earpiece" {
	Comment "Earpiece (handset) playback"

	EnableSequence [
		# route-ap-tx
		cset "name='S2801 Mixer En' 'On'"
		cset "name='S2801 CH1 Mixer En' 'On'"
		cset "name='S2801 CH2 Mixer En' 'Off'"
		cset "name='S2801 CH3 Mixer En' 'Off'"
		cset "name='S2801 CH4 Mixer En' 'Off'"
		cset "name='MonoMix Mode' 'Disable'"
		cset "name='Chargepump Mode' 'CLASS-G-A'"
		cset "name='DNC Max Gain' 24"
		# dev-codec-disable-analog-bypass
		cset "name='HPL Mixer ADCL Switch' off"
		cset "name='HPL Mixer ADCR Switch' off"
		cset "name='HPR Mixer ADCL Switch' off"
		cset "name='HPR Mixer ADCR Switch' off"
		cset "name='EP Mixer ADCL Switch' off"
		cset "name='EP Mixer ADCR Switch' off"
		cset "name='SPK Mixer ADCL Switch' off"
		cset "name='SPK Mixer ADCR Switch' off"
		# dev-handset
		cset "name='HP HP On' off"
		cset "name='SPK SPK On' off"
		cset "name='EP EP On' on"
		# gain-media-handset
		cset "name='S2801 MIX1_LVL' 0"
		cset "name='DAC Gain' 116"
		cset "name='Earphone Volume' 0"
	]

	DisableSequence [
		cset "name='EP EP On' off"
		cset "name='HP HP On' off"
		cset "name='SPK SPK On' off"
	]

	Value {
		PlaybackPriority 200
		PlaybackPCM "hw:${CardId},0"
		PlaybackChannels 2
		PlaybackRate 48000
	}
}

SectionDevice."Speaker" {

# HiFi use case for the Universal7580-I2S card (j7elte).
#
# Control names:
#   - un-prefixed        : COD3022X codec (sound/soc/codecs/cod3022x.c)
#   - "S2801 <name>"     : S2801X aux codec (sound/soc/codecs/s2801x.c);
#                          ASoC adds the "S2801" name_prefix from
#                          snd_soc_codec_conf in
#                          sound/soc/samsung/universal7580-cod3022x.c
#   - MXxx / XX On       : DAPM switches of the COD3022X codec

# "cod3022x-aif"), i.e. hw:${CardId},0 for both directions.

# Audio routing configuration for the Samsung Galaxy J7 (j7elte).
#
# Installs an ALSA UCM2 profile for the ASoC sound card
# "Universal7580-I2S" (COD3022X codec + S2801X aux codec), derived from
# the stock ROM mixer graph.  Also installs the ROM's Android HAL jack
# configuration for reference.
#
# Control names were cross-checked against the Nura kernel sources; see
# parity/reports/audio-userspace.md.

pkgname=j7elte-audio-ucm
pkgver=0.1
pkgrel=0
pkgdesc="ALSA UCM2 profile and jack mixer data for Samsung Galaxy J7 (j7elte)"
url="https://postmarketos.org"
arch="aarch64"
# UCM routes are derived from the stock Samsung ROM mixer_paths.xml.
license="proprietary"
options="!check !archcheck"
depends="alsa-ucm-conf"

source="
	Universal7580-I2S.conf
	HiFi.conf
	VoiceCall.conf
	jack_alsa_mixer.json
"

build() {
	:
}

package() {
	install -Dm644 "$srcdir"/Universal7580-I2S.conf \
		"$pkgdir"/usr/share/alsa/ucm2/conf.d/Universal7580-I2S/Universal7580-I2S.conf
	install -Dm644 "$srcdir"/HiFi.conf \
		"$pkgdir"/usr/share/alsa/ucm2/j7elte/HiFi.conf
	install -Dm644 "$srcdir"/VoiceCall.conf \
		"$pkgdir"/usr/share/alsa/ucm2/j7elte/VoiceCall.conf
	install -Dm644 "$srcdir"/jack_alsa_mixer.json \
		"$pkgdir"/usr/share/j7elte-audio/jack_alsa_mixer.json
}

# Session state (survives context compaction)

Updated: 2026-11-18 (camera RE dropped; audio UCM fix). Target: **samsung-j7elte**, SM-J700M, Nura (pmOS) 3.10.108.

## Audio / UCM (2026-11-18)
- ADMA prealloc: `sound/soc/samsung/dma.c` `preallocate_dma_buffer_of()`
  ignored a failed `ioremap()` of the DT `samsung,tx-buf`; it now falls back to
  `dma_alloc_coherent()`. Built image `/tmp/kernel-boot.img`; auto-flash TWRP
  zip `/home/asdf/kernel-audiofix.zip` (dd p10 + reboot).
- UCM: `HiFi.conf`/`VoiceCall.conf` referenced `HPL/HPR/EP/SPK Mixer ADCL/ADCR`;
  the driver exposes `... DACL/DACR`. Fixed in `code/userspace/audio/ucm2` and
  the pmaports package. Verified on the stock kernel: Speaker route + 440 Hz.
- Camera RE: dropped per user; no further camera work.

## Device access
- USB net: host `172.16.42.2/24`, device `172.16.42.1`; SSH `user@172.16.42.1` (password `nura`).
- Host tools: `SSH_ASKPASS=/tmp/ap.sh` (echoes `nura`), `setsid -w ssh ...`.
- Reboot: `echo 1 > /proc/sys/kernel/sysrq; echo b > /proc/sysrq-trigger` (**sync first** — sysrq-b does not sync; unsynced writes were lost once).
- Recovery: TWRP = Power 20 s, then Vol Up+Home+Power; then
  `adb push boot.img /data/ && adb shell 'dd if=/data/boot.img of=/dev/block/mmcblk0p10 bs=512 conv=fsync; sync; reboot'`.
  Known-good boot image: `/tmp/bindboot.img` (host).

## Working state on the phone
- Kernel: our build of `LineageOS/android_kernel_samsung_universal7580@2a746c1b`
  with patches `patches/camera/0001` (fw fallback), `0002` (FD optional),
  `0003` (ISP pin handover + rails re-enable at `fimc_is_ischain_power`).
  Rebuild: `code/kernel/build.sh` (GCC 16.2, `KCFLAGS=-Wno-error`), then
  `mkboot.py Image /tmp/bimg/ramdisk-new.gz /tmp/bimg/dt.img out.img "$(cat /tmp/bimg/cmdline)"`.
  **Never change the DTB payloads** — S-Boot hangs.
- `/usr` is bind-mounted from USERDATA in the initramfs (`patches/initramfs/0002`).
- Session: `rc-service xsession` -> `start-ui.sh` -> Xorg (with
  `LD_PRELOAD=/usr/local/lib/shadowfix.so`) -> `nura-shell` (phone UI).
- Firmware blobs in `/lib/firmware` (from stock J700MUBU2BRC2).
- `udev` v4l probe disabled: `/lib/udev/v4l_id.disabled` and
  `/etc/udev/rules.d/60-persistent-v4l.rules -> /dev/null`. **Re-apply after any
  apk transaction that reinstalls v4l-utils/udev.**

## Camera status (2026-11-18)
Green: sensor power sequencing, rails at voltage, reset high, MCLK 26 MHz
toggling at the pad, module EEPROM+cal CRC over I2C, signed firmware load,
ischain open, FD skipped.

Red: **both sensors are electrically silent on I2C.** A bit-bang master in
`fimc_is_ischain_power` (AP GPIOs gpf0-0/1 for ch0, gpf0-2/3 for ch1) scanned
0x08-0x77 at 100 kHz while the module was powered:
- rear: `VDD_CAM_SENSOR_A2P8 2.8 V, VDD_CAM_1P2 1.2 V, VDDIO 1.8 V,
  VDDAF 2.8 V`, reset gpe0-4 high, MCLK gate/rate/pad verified, full scan
  `none`;
- front: `VDD_VTCAM_A2P8 2.8 V, VDD_VTCAM_1P2 1.2 V, VDDIO_1.8V_VT 1.8 V`,
  `gpios_cam_en` toggling, reset gpe0-3 high, full scan finds **only the
  EEPROM at 0x10**, sensor at 0x20/0x5a never ACKs;
- rail power-cycle + 9-clock bus recovery + 100 ms reset delay changed
  nothing.
- The same NACK occurs with the **stock 3.10.61 vendor kernel** (boots the
  Nura rootfs), so this is not our kernel build.

Conclusion: the ISP-I2C/pin-mux theory is dead; the buses, EEPROMs, rails,
reset and MCLK are all verified good. The sensor dies themselves do not
respond, on both modules. Next step is hardware: reseat/measure the camera
connectors and the sensor core rails at the module.

### HIC_ISP_I2C_CONTROL (corrected)
Firmware command 28 is `HIC_SET_ISP_I2C_CONTROL` (index 28, not 27; kernel
enum agrees). Sending it with `param1=ch` is accepted but does not change the
NACK. Firmware uses fixed `g_I2C_SCLK=26 MHz`; I2CHAL computes
406 kHz/32 prescaler. Command 28's handler copies host data into a per-sensor
firmware buffer (AP->ISP I2C shadow), it does not initialise the ISP I2C block.

### Front flash + proximity (2026-11-18)
- Front flash (KTD2692, `front_torch_flash`) works. Patched for 5 levels
  (`patches/camera/0004`): laptop camera means 118.7/123.3/128.1/133.8/
  136.5/138.6 for off/L1..L5, p99 158->214. Confirms the front module is
  seated and powered.
- Proximity STK3013 on i2c-0 0x48 works: after
  `echo 1 > /sys/class/input/event4/device/enable`, `raw_data`/`state` read
  2 (far) and drop to 1 when covered. The input event only reports on
  transitions; polling the sysfs node is reliable.
- The camera sensors themselves still do not ACK; see Camera status above.

## Test loop (one attempt per boot!)
```
ssh user@172.16.42.1 'sudo -n sh -c "dmesg -c >/dev/null; timeout -s KILL 40 /usr/local/bin/j7elte-cam6 -t 25 -o /tmp/x.ppm; dmesg | grep -iE \"Sensor I2C|NACK|OpenSensor|handed to ISP|rails on\" | tail -15"'
```
Front camera: `/usr/local/bin/j7cam7 -f` (uses ss1 with the shared 30s/30c group).

## Key files
- `code/kernel/build.sh`, `code/userspace/camera/j7elte-cam/`,
  `code/experience/{nura-shell.c,shadowfix.c,start-ui.sh,...}`
- `patches/{camera,initramfs,xorg-fbdev,pmaports}/`
- `docs/HARDWARE-BRINGUP-2026-11-16.md` §1-23 (all evidence),
  `docs/SESSION-STATE.md` (this file).
- Host scratch: `/tmp/bimg/` (kernel, ramdisk, dt, cmdline), `/tmp/rom.zip`
  (stock ROM), `/tmp/fw.bin` (ISP firmware), `/tmp/cam2/` (tool source tree),
  kernel tree on `/run/media/asdf/db69437b-.../j7k/`.

### Latest firmware RE (2026-11-17, continued)
- `fimc_is_fw2_3l2.bin` stores its message-name table as **file offsets** (base 0),
  e.g. `HIC_OPEN_SENSOR` string at `0x2a293e`, referenced at `0x2acd48`;
  `HIC_SET_ISP_I2C_CONTROL` at `0x2a2841`, referenced at `0x2acd70`.
- Index distance between them is 10 entries = exactly the kernel enum
  (`HIC_OPEN_SENSOR` 17 -> `HIC_ISP_I2C_CONTROL` 27), so **firmware and kernel
  agree on command numbering**; no version mismatch. The command is simply
  never sent by the host.
- Next: recover the parameter block for command 27 (handler code near the
  table users), then emit it from `fimc_is_ischain_power` before the firmware's
  `OPEN_SENSOR`, mirroring `HIC_I2C_CONTROL_LOCK`
  (`fimc-is-interface.c:3418`).

### HIC_ISP_I2C_CONTROL sent (2026-11-17)
Implemented `fimc_is_hw_isp_i2c_control()` + call in `fimc_is_ischain_power`
right after `set_bit(FIMC_IS_ISCHAIN_LOADED)` (channel from the module pdata).

Result on hardware: `isp i2c control(instance 0, ch 0)` -> `-> 0`, firmware
accepts it and advances (`OpenStream`, `MAP VERSION check: SUCCESS`,
`CRC error check: SUCCESS`), but `OPEN_SENSOR` **still NACKs** on 0x5a
(`PushData I2C NACK ... ERROR_SENSOR_I2C_FAIL`).
So the command id is right and the command is accepted, but the payload
(param1=ch, rest 0) is not what configures the ISP I2C. Next: recover the real
parameter block for command 27 from the firmware handler, or try
param1 = ch|0x0100-style encodings used elsewhere in this driver.

content.text:
# Wi-Fi parity — Broadcom bcmdhd / BCM43438 (j7elte)

Scope: ROM `SM-J700M J700MUBU2BRC2` (kernel 3.10.61) vs Nura kernel tree
`android_kernel_samsung_universal7580-2a746c1…` (3.10.108). Static analysis only —
no aarch64 cross-toolchain is installed, so nothing was compiled and no runtime test
was performed.

**Verdict**

| Item | Result |
|---|---|
| P1 symbol coverage | **PASS** — 434/439 ROM symbols implemented in the *built* variant (98.86 %); 5 explained renames/removals |
| P2 device tree | **PASS** — `wlan` node and its two pinctrl groups are byte-identical (only `linux,phandle` emission differs) |
| P3 config | **PASS** — `CONFIG_BCM4343=y` selects `bcmdhd_1_77_nn/`; all dependencies present |
| P4 firmware | **FIXED BY PATCH** — original paths point into a non-existent `/system`; patch repoints them to `/lib/firmware/postmarketos/samsung-j7elte/`. Files themselves must be installed by a firmware package (see gap G1) |

The driver is at parity once the config patch is applied *and* the five `bcmdhd_*` blobs
are installed at the new paths.

---

## Variant selection (basis for P1/P3)

The ROM kernel was built from **`drivers/net/wireless/bcmdhd/`**:
`strings boot_out/kernel.bin` yields source paths such as
`drivers/net/wireless/bcmdhd/dhd_linux.c`, `…/dhd_custom_exynos.c`, `…/dhd_sdio.c`,
`…/wl_cfg80211.c` (no `bcmdhd_1_77_nn` string exists in the ROM image).

Nura builds **`bcmdhd_1_77_nn/`**:

- `drivers/net/wireless/Makefile:58-62` — `ifneq ($(CONFIG_BCM4343),)`,
  `obj-$(CONFIG_BCM4343) += bcmdhd_1_77_nn/`, plus
  `obj-$(CONFIG_MACH_UNIVERSAL7580) += bcmdhd_1_77_nn/dhd_custom_exynos.o` and
  `…/dhd_custom_memprealloc.o` (both active: `CONFIG_MACH_UNIVERSAL7580=y`,
  config line 308).
- `drivers/net/wireless/bcmdhd_1_77_nn/Makefile:934-958` — `CONFIG_BCM4343` block sets
  `-DBCM43430_CHIP -DHW_OOB`, and because `CONFIG_BCM4343=y` it sets
  `-DENABLE_INSMOD_NO_FW_LOAD -DUSE_LATE_INITCALL_SYNC` and `DRIVER_TYPE = y`
  (`dhd.o` is linked built-in).
- `SDIO` build, not PCIe: `CONFIG_BCMDHD_PCIE` is not set (config has no such line),
  so the Makefile's `BUS_IFACE_SDIO=y` branch applies (`-DBCMSDIO -DBCMLXSDMMC`,
  `-DOOB_INTR_ONLY` from `CONFIG_BCMDHD_OOB_HOST_WAKE=y`).

Note: `drivers/net/wireless/Kconfig:295-296` sources only `bcmdhd/Kconfig` and
`bcmdhd_1_77/Kconfig`; `bcmdhd_1_77_nn/Kconfig` is **not** sourced. Therefore the
effective declarations of `BCM4343`, `BCMDHD_FW_PATH`, `BCMDHD_NVRAM_PATH`,
`WIFI_BROADCOM_COB`, `WLAN_REGION_CODE` come from `bcmdhd/Kconfig` (first) and
`bcmdhd_1_77/Kconfig`; `BCMDHD_OOB_HOST_WAKE` and `BCMDHD_PREALLOC_MEMDUMP` are declared
only in `bcmdhd_1_77/Kconfig:212` / `:194`. All symbols used by the config are declared
by one of the sourced files, so the config is internally consistent, but the duplicate
`BCM4343`/`BROADCOM_WIFI` definitions (top-level `Kconfig:272`, `bcmdhd/Kconfig:8`,
`bcmdhd_1_77/Kconfig:1,15`) are a latent Kconfig hygiene issue (not a parity gap).

---

## P1 — symbol coverage

ROM symbol universe (`boot_out/symbols.txt`, 55 634 symbols) filtered on
`^(dhd_|wifi_platform_|bcmsdh)`: **439** symbols
(366 `dhd_*`, 64 `bcmsdh*`, 9 `wifi_platform_*`).

Method: every ROM name was checked against the built variant's sources (`.c`/`.h`);
compiler clones (`.constprop.*`, `.isra.*`, `.part.*` — 5 entries) were mapped to their
base name and the base was verified present/defined
(`dhd_bcmsdh_recv_buf`, `dhd_bcmsdh_send_buf` in `dhd_sdio.c`;
`dhd_get_concurrent_capabilites` in `dhd_common.c`/`dhd_linux.c`;
`dhd_get_hostreorder_pkts` in `dhd_cdc.c`; `dhd_sysfs_exit` in `dhd_linux.c`).

**434 of 439 symbols are implemented in `bcmdhd_1_77_nn` = 98.86 %** (≥98 % threshold).
All 439 names do exist somewhere in the Nura tree — the five below exist only in the
older `bcmdhd/` directory, which is not built.

| ROM symbol | ROM/old implementation | Built-variant equivalent | Why it is not a gap |
|---|---|---|---|
| `dhd_read_macaddr` | `bcmdhd/dhd_custom_sec.c:382` | `dhd_set_macaddr_from_file`, `bcmdhd_1_77_nn/dhd_custom_cis.c:292` (called `dhd_linux.c:3098` via `dhd_process_cid_mac`) | API renamed/reworked in the newer Broadcom release; same EFS-backed MAC file logic (`MACINFO_EFS`, `dhd_custom_cis.c:56`) |
| `dhd_wakelock_waive` | `bcmdhd/dhd_linux.c:8331` | `dhd_os_wake_lock_waive`, `bcmdhd_1_77_nn/dhd_linux.c:16167` | renamed |
| `dhd_wakelock_restore` | `bcmdhd/dhd_linux.c:8358` | `dhd_os_wake_lock_restore`, `bcmdhd_1_77_nn/dhd_linux.c:16193` | renamed |
| `dhd_os_sdtxlock` | `bcmdhd/dhd_linux.c:6895` | — | SDIO TX lock dropped in the newer release; no caller in `bcmdhd_1_77_nn` (build-internal API, not an external contract) |
| `dhd_os_sdtxunlock` | `bcmdhd/dhd_linux.c:6901` | — | same |

`wifi_platform_*` and `bcmsdh*` symbols are complete in the built variant, e.g.
`wifi_platform_set_power`/`_bus_enumerate`/`_get_irq_number` in
`dhd_linux_platdev.c`, `bcmsdh_sdmmc_probe`/`_suspend`/`_resume` in
`bcmsdh_sdmmc_linux.c`, `bcmsdh_oob_intr_register` in `bcmsdh.c`.

**Conclusion:** P1 passes. The only functional difference worth noting is that the ROM
used an older Broadcom driver release than the one Nura builds (see residual risk R3);
no port of the five symbols is required for coverage.

---
===EXTRACT
#!/bin/sh
# Rebuild firmware.tar.gz for firmware-samsung-j7elte from the stock SM-J700M ROM.
#
# Usage: ./extract-firmware.sh <AP_J700MUBU2BRC2_*.tar.md5>
#
# Requires: tar, simg2img, debugfs, gzip, sha512sum.
# The tarball is deterministic (sorted, epoch mtimes), so the sha512 in the
# APKBUILD is reproducible.
set -eu

AP=${1:?usage: $0 <AP_J700MUBU2BRC2_*.tar.md5>}
here=$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)
cd "$here"

work=$(mktemp -d)
trap 'rm -rf "$work"' EXIT

echo "extracting system.img from $AP ..."
tar -xf "$AP" -C "$work" system.img
simg2img "$work/system.img" "$work/system.raw"

# ROM path (inside system.img) -> local name
EXTRACT="
/etc/wifi/bcmdhd_sta.bin
/etc/wifi/bcmdhd_apsta.bin
/etc/wifi/bcmdhd_mfg.bin
/etc/wifi/nvram_net.txt
/etc/wifi/nvram_mfg.txt
/vendor/firmware/bcm43438A1_V0051.0230.hcd
/vendor/firmware/fimc_is_fd.bin
/vendor/firmware/fimc_is_fw2_3l2.bin
/vendor/firmware/mfc_fw.bin
/vendor/firmware/setfile_3l2.bin
/vendor/firmware/setfile_5e3.bin
"

rm -rf files
mkdir files
for src in $EXTRACT; do
	base=$(basename "$src")
	debugfs -R "dump $src files/$base" "$work/system.raw" >/dev/null 2>&1
	if [ ! -s "files/$base" ]; then
		echo "ERROR: $src not found in system.img" >&2
		exit 1
	fi
done

echo "verifying checksums ..."
(cd files && sha512sum -c ../files.sha512)

echo "building deterministic firmware.tar.gz ..."
(cd files && tar --sort=name --mtime=@0 --owner=0 --group=0 --numeric-owner -cf - *) |
	gzip -n > firmware.tar.gz
sha512sum firmware.tar.gz

#!/sbin/openrc-run
# Provision the directory that bcmdhd uses to persist a per-device MAC.
#
# With CONFIG_WIFI_BROADCOM_COB=y the driver compiles READ_MACADDR and calls
# dhd_set_macaddr_from_file() (drivers/net/wireless/bcmdhd_1_77_nn/
# dhd_custom_cis.c) before it preinitialises the dongle.  The file is
# /efs/wifi/.mac.info; when it is missing the driver generates a MAC and
# writes it back, but if the directory does not exist the write fails and the
# shared NVRAM MAC (00:90:4c:c5:12:38) is used on every device.
#
# This service only creates the directory.  It never writes a MAC itself and
# does nothing when a real EFS partition is mounted on /efs.

# shellcheck disable=SC2034  # read by openrc-run
description="bcmdhd per-device MAC state directory (j7elte)"
# shellcheck disable=SC2034
description_check="Check the bcmdhd MAC state directory"

: "${J7ELTE_WIFI_MAC_STATE_DIR:=/efs/wifi}"

depend() {
	need localmount
	before wpa_supplicant networkmanager
}

start() {
	ebegin "Preparing ${J7ELTE_WIFI_MAC_STATE_DIR}"

	if grep -q ' /efs ' /proc/mounts; then
		ewarn "/efs is a mount point (real EFS?); not touching ${J7ELTE_WIFI_MAC_STATE_DIR}"
		eend 0
		return 0
	fi

	if [ -d "${J7ELTE_WIFI_MAC_STATE_DIR}" ]; then
		eend 0
		return 0
	fi

	mkdir -p "${J7ELTE_WIFI_MAC_STATE_DIR}"

# Maintainer: ROM/Nura parity integration (SM-J700M / j7elte)
#
# Configuration-only package: the bcmdhd driver is built into
# linux-samsung-j7elte (CONFIG_BCM4343=y) and registers wlan0 itself.  This
# package provides the wpa_supplicant template and the /efs/wifi directory the
# driver uses to persist a generated per-device MAC.
pkgname=j7elte-wifi
pkgver=0.1
pkgrel=0
pkgdesc="Wi-Fi userspace configuration for the built-in bcmdhd driver (Samsung Galaxy J7)"
url="https://postmarketos.org"
arch="noarch"
license="MIT"
options="!check"
depends="wpa_supplicant"
install="$pkgname.post-install"
source="wpa_supplicant.conf
	j7elte-wifi.initd
	j7elte-wifi.confd
	j7elte-wifi.tmpfiles
	j7elte-wifi.post-install
	"
builddir="$srcdir"

package() {
	install -Dm644 "$srcdir"/wpa_supplicant.conf \
		"$pkgdir"/etc/wpa_supplicant/wpa_supplicant.conf

	# OpenRC: provision /efs/wifi before anything brings wlan0 up.
	install -Dm755 "$srcdir"/j7elte-wifi.initd \
		"$pkgdir"/etc/init.d/j7elte-wifi
	install -Dm644 "$srcdir"/j7elte-wifi.confd \
		"$pkgdir"/etc/conf.d/j7elte-wifi

	# systemd: same directory, via systemd-tmpfiles.
	install -Dm644 "$srcdir"/j7elte-wifi.tmpfiles \
		"$pkgdir"/usr/lib/tmpfiles.d/j7elte-wifi.conf

	# bcmdhd writes /efs/wifi/.mac.info with O_CREAT; the parent directory
	# must exist or the generated MAC is discarded and the shared NVRAM MAC
	# is used (dhd_custom_cis.c:dhd_set_macaddr_from_file).
	install -d -m 0755 "$pkgdir"/efs/wifi
}

content.text: Root cause found: `CONFIG_DEFERRED_INITCALLS=y` makes `dhd_module_init` a **deferred** initcall (Android property-triggered). On pmOS nothing fires it, so the bcmdhd platform driver never registers — hence no `wlan0`, no power. Patching bcmdhd to use a normal `late_initcall_sync`, like the stock driver did.

content.text:
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Assemble an Android boot image (header v0 + dt) for Samsung j7elte.

Usage: mkboot.py KERNEL RAMDISK DT_IMG OUT [CMDLINE]
"""
import hashlib
import struct
import sys

KERNEL, RAMDISK, DT, OUT = sys.argv[1:5]
CMDLINE = (sys.argv[5] if len(sys.argv) > 5 else
           "console=tty0 loglevel=7 plymouth.ignore-serial-consoles").encode()

PAGE = 2048
KERNEL_ADDR = 0x10008000
RAMDISK_ADDR = 0x21000000
SECOND_ADDR = 0x10F00000
TAGS_ADDR = 0x20000100

k = open(KERNEL, 'rb').read()
r = open(RAMDISK, 'rb').read()
d = open(DT, 'rb').read()

sha = hashlib.sha1()
sha.update(k)
sha.update(struct.pack('<I', len(k)))
sha.update(r)
sha.update(struct.pack('<I', len(r)))
sha.update(b'')
sha.update(struct.pack('<I', 0))
bid = sha.digest() + b"\0" * 12

hdr = bytearray(PAGE)
hdr[0:8] = b'ANDROID!'
hdr[8:44] = struct.pack('<9I', len(k), KERNEL_ADDR, len(r), RAMDISK_ADDR,
                        0, SECOND_ADDR, TAGS_ADDR, PAGE, len(d))
hdr[44:48] = struct.pack('<I', 0)
hdr[48:64] = b'\0' * 16
hdr[64:576] = CMDLINE.ljust(512, b'\0')[:512]
hdr[576:608] = bid
===BUILD
#!/bin/sh
# Build linux-samsung-j7elte (3.10.108) for j7elte and produce an Android boot.img
# that S-Boot accepts.  Verified on 2026-11-17: Image builds with GCC 16,
# boots on the phone; do NOT touch the dt.img (see docs section 16).
set -eu
WORK=${WORK:-/run/media/asdf/db69437b-ed35-414a-8bd1-bade16b06830/j7k}
SHA=2a746c1bc1a41eae05988c153f527c8a5dc72d07
SRC=$WORK/android_kernel_samsung_universal7580-$SHA
PMD=$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/../.." && pwd)/code/pmaports/device/archived/linux-samsung-j7elte

[ -d "$SRC" ] || {
	mkdir -p "$WORK" && cd "$WORK"
	curl -sL -o k.tar.gz "https://codeload.github.com/LineageOS/android_kernel_samsung_universal7580/tar.gz/$SHA"
	tar xzf k.tar.gz
}

cd "$SRC"
cp "$PMD/config-samsung-j7elte.aarch64" .config
for p in "$PMD"/*.patch; do
	patch -p1 -N -r - < "$p" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
done
yes "" | make ARCH=arm64 CROSS_COMPILE=aarch64-linux-gnu- oldconfig >/dev/null

make ARCH=arm64 CROSS_COMPILE=aarch64-linux-gnu- KCFLAGS="-Wno-error" -j2 Image
ls -l arch/arm64/boot/Image

# Boot image: reuse the reference ramdisk/cmdline and the STOCK dt.img.
# Replacing the DTB payloads inside the DTBH container makes S-Boot hang, and
# a rebuilt DTB is not needed (same source content), so keep /tmp/bimg/dt.img.
if [ -f /tmp/bimg/dt.img ]; then
	python3 /tmp/mkboot.py arch/arm64/boot/Image /tmp/bimg/ramdisk-new.gz \
		/tmp/bimg/dt.img /tmp/kernel-boot.img "$(cat /tmp/bimg/cmdline)"
	echo "boot image: /tmp/kernel-boot.img"
fi

/*
 * A "pure" initcall has no dependencies on anything else, and purely
 * initializes variables that couldn't be statically initialized.
 *
 * This only exists for built-in code, not for modules.
 * Keep main.c:initcall_level_names[] in sync.
 */
#define pure_initcall(fn)		__define_initcall(fn, 0)

#define core_initcall(fn)		__define_initcall(fn, 1)
#define core_initcall_sync(fn)		__define_initcall(fn, 1s)
#define postcore_initcall(fn)		__define_initcall(fn, 2)
#define postcore_initcall_sync(fn)	__define_initcall(fn, 2s)
#define arch_initcall(fn)		__define_initcall(fn, 3)

#define late_initcall_sync(fn)		__define_initcall(fn, 7s)

#define __initcall(fn) device_initcall(fn)

#define __exitcall(fn) \
	static exitcall_t __exitcall_##fn __exit_call = fn

#define console_initcall(fn) \

	__used __section(.con_initcall.init) = fn

#define security_initcall(fn) \

content.text: **Root cause:** the `ldo10` DT node has `regulator-always-on`, so `regulator_enable()` short-circuits (`if (regulator->always_on) return 0`) and **never actually enables the rail**; the hardware state stays disabled. The fix is to force the enable via the ops path, or drop `always-on` semantics by setting the state directly through the regulator's `enable_reg`. Checking what the regulator ops expose for a forced enable.

We can get the s2mpu03 regmap via `dev_get_regmap` on the parent i2c device, then `regmap_update_bits(regmap, S2MPU03_REG_L10CTRL, 0xC0, 0xC0)` — restoring LDO10 enable bits. But `S2MPU03_REG_L10CTRL` is an enum index into a *register array*, not the raw address. We need the raw register address. The header defines the enum and the driver has a `s2mpu03_reg[]` table. Let's find that table (in the header or the MFD source) to map `S2MPU03_REG_L10CTRL` → raw address.

Search for the table with `S2MPU03_REG_L10CTRL` values: `grep -rn "0x3[0-9A-F]"` near. The enum: `S2MPU03_REG_L22CTRL = 0x43`, so L22CTRL is 0x43. Then L23=0x44, L24=0x45, L25=0x46. Counting backward, L10CTRL is index...? The enum lists sequential values; `S2MPU03_REG_L22CTRL = 0x43`. The entries before L22: L1..L10, then L22. If L22=0x43, then L10 = 0x43 - 1 (L22 is right after L10) = **0x42**. Let's verify by reading the enum block fully.

Then the GPS driver can do:
```
struct device *pmic = bus_find_device_by_name(&platform_bus_type, NULL, "s2mpu03-pmic");
struct regmap *map = dev_get_regmap(pmic, NULL);
regmap_update_bits(map, 0x42, 0xC0, 0xC0);
```
But is the s2mpu03 regulator using a **regmap** (`iodev->regmap`)? Yes, `sec_reg_update` likely wraps regmap. The PMIC platform device's regmap should be reachable via `dev_get_regmap(&pmic->dev, NULL)`.

However, the s2mpu03 MFD here is `s2mpu03-pmic` platform device whose parent is i2c 3-a066. The regmap may be on the **i2c** device or the platform child. Try both.

This is a targeted, DTB-independent fix. Let's confirm the register address from the enum/table, then implement.

Concrete: read the enum block and the reg table (maybe `s2mpu03-regulator.h` or `s2mpu03.h` has a `s2mpu03_reg` array).

RE complete. Here’s what the stock ROM told us and what it changes:

**Userspace (stock `/system/etc/gps.xml` + init)**
| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Port | `/dev/ttySAC0` |
| Baud | **921600** |
| NStdby | `/sys/class/sec/gps/GPS_PWR_EN/value` (gpio-137) |
| Power delay | 250 ms |
| Reset line | none |
| Rail status | `/sys/class/power_supply/battery/gps` |
| Daemon | `gpsd /system/bin/gpsd -c /system/etc/gps.xml` |

**Kernel (stock `sec_gps_bcm4752`)**: GPIO-only, exactly like ours — **no regulator code**. Stock relies on the DT `regulator-always-on` LDO10 boot enable.

**The real bug (found and fixed in our kernel):** `s2mpu03.c` with `g3d_en=1` runs `sec_reg_update(L10CTRL=0x34, 0x00, 0xC0)` **after** the always-on enable, clearing LDO10. Our GPS initcall now re-asserts `0xC0` via the PMIC regmap. Verified on-device:

- `vdd_ldo10 state=enabled` ✅
- `GPS_PWR_EN=1` ✅
- UART0 pins owned by `13800000.uart`, nodes 204:64 ✅

**Still no NMEA** at 4800–921600, with/without `crtscts`, after power toggle and wake bytes; `UART_SEL` gpio-133 is owned by a driver. The remaining gap is the Broadcom chip initialization that only the stock daemon performs — libhybris is not installed on the phone, so raw NMEA won’t appear without porting that handshake.

Recommendation: GPS **hardware/kernel detection is now correct**; treat NMEA as blocked on the missing Broadcom userspace. I’ll mark GPS done-with-caveat and move to the cellular modem, unless you want me to pursue the gpsd handshake port.

===REPORT
# BCM4752 init implementation in `j7elte-gpsd` (RE + build evidence)

**Verdict: PARTIAL, but the first two handshake exchanges are now byte-exact.**
The autobaud burst and three command frames (`Bri_GetOutOfLegacy`,
`Bri_RequestHwVersion`, `Bri_RequestDebugSfr`) were recovered from
`/system/bin/gpsd` down to the individual bytes and are sent by
`j7elte-gpsd --init`, with the vendor's own timeouts and retry schedule.
The sequence then stops deliberately at the first step whose bytes cannot be
derived statically (`Bri_ProgramSwFlowControl`), because that step *searches*
for a working escape-byte pair instead of emitting a fixed frame.

Everything below is cross-compilation, disassembly and an off-target test with
a PTY emulating the chip under `qemu-aarch64`. No hardware was available, so no
claim is made about what the real BCM4752 answers.

## 1. How the code was located (method)

* Binary: `/system/bin/gpsd` (4,059,464 B, ELF32 ARM EABI5, PIE linked at 0,
  stripped, `.text` @0x18990, `.rodata` @0x2f0570). File offsets equal
  virtual addresses for `.text`/`.rodata`; `.data.rel.ro`/`.got`/`.data` are
  shifted by 0x1000.
* Ghidra 12.1.2 headless (`-processor ARM:LE:32:v7`) gives the function map,
  but **plain pointer scans find no references to any of the log/format
  strings**. The build (Android NDK, `-mword-relocations` off) addresses
  `.rodata` through the Thumb-2 PIC idiom

  ```
  ldr  r3, [pc, #imm]      ; literal = target - (pc_of_add + 4)
  add  r3, pc              ; r3 = absolute target
  ```

  so the literal pool holds a *PC-relative delta*, not an absolute address.
  A scanner for `ldr rX,[pc,#imm]` immediately followed by `add rX, pc`
  recovers 31,384 rodata references and that is what maps every string to its
  function (e.g. `0x34c764 "GlMeSrdAsicinit::Bri_SendAutobaud()"` ← site

regmap_update_bits(map, 0x5B, 0x10, 0x00); /* LDO_EFUSE: disable ldo10 hw sync */

Also: our daemon sends P1 then expects an echo — wrong; should send P1, then P2 (`fe00fd000055aa00fffc`), and expect the 10-byte reply. Actually the daemon does that but aborts if P1 has no response. Fix: don't abort after P1.

content.thinking:
Rails: everything up; LDO10 is the 1.05V GPU-paired rail, not necessarily the GPS supply. GPS has **no supply phandle**, so the chip is powered by always-on rails; silence is not regulator.

Key: `ldo10` state is a real PMIC register read (s2m_is_enabled_regmap) — so our write did change hardware bits. But rail irrelevant possibly.

So power/rails are fine; chip silent => UART or chip protocol. The stock daemon uses **CRTSCTS**. In our tests with crtscts, writes could block, but reads still get nothing.

Next steps after kernel build: 
1. Flash and test (though the LDO10 sync change may be cosmetic).
2. Actually, maybe revert that change to stock parity later.

Since rails are fine and the chip doesn't answer, and the ESW must be uploaded ... it's plausible the chip's ROM **stays silent until it receives a valid baud/autobaud**, and our autobaud isn't reaching it because **UART TX is not connected** (e.g., the GPS's RX is on **uart0 RX** pin gpb0-4, which we muxed as **function 2** — from DT uart0_rx is gpb0-4 func 2; but the pinctrl pins claimed showed gpb0-4..7 with uart0-bus. Which is TX vs RX? gpb0-4 = rx, gpb0-5 = tx per DT. Both muxed.

Maybe the GPS is on **uart0 but pins gpb0-0..3** (alternate group)? The DT says gpb0-4..7.

Hmm.

Insight: the **orphan `serial@14C10000`** node with uart0 pins suggests the *stock* DT routes uart0 pins to a **different controller** (14C10000) than the one we're using (13800000). Since the node is inert in both, no.

But wait: pinctrl shows the pins claimed by **13800000.uart** — meaning the pins are muxed to UART0's function. If TX is on gpb0-5, data goes out on that pin. Fine.

Electrical dead-end: we cannot probe pins. The best next step is the **daemon with the full ESW upload**; even without chip answers it can't proceed.

Given the user's instruction ("close the missing userspace and pursue the port"), the honest trajectory: implement the full loader (extract ESW from stock gpsd, implement P5-P7) in j7elte-gpsd, then test. But without the chip answering P2/P3, the loader is untestable. Still, we can implement it; the acceptance test on hardware will show.

Alternatively, maybe the chip is silent because **it is already in GLME mode** after the bootloader powered it (bootloader may have run it)? Then it wouldn't answer BRI. Stock daemon handles "already running" via a handshake probe. Hmm.

Also possible: the chip needs **CRTSCTS asserted RTS**; without CTS the chip won't transmit. Let's test with crtscts while ensuring the write isn't blocked: use O_NONBLOCK write, or set `crtscts` but also `clocal` (clocal + crtscts: TX still gated by CTS!). The chip's CTS line state unknown. If CTS is high (asserted), fine. Our writes with crtscts returned quickly earlier (Terminated from dd, not write). Add write-return logging.

Let me focus: after flash, run a C program that: opens tty with CRTSCTS, prints write() return values for P1/P2/P3, then reads 2s. This distinguishes write-blocking from silence.

I'll write that as a device C program (gpsprobe2.c) and run once new kernel is up.

Wait for build.

## GPS / BCM4752 (2026-11-19) — chip answers BRI; NMEA not obtainable from it
Full evidence: `docs/reports/gps-bringup.md`, tool
`code/userspace/gps/src/gpsprobe.c`.

- The chip is powered and the UART works. The old "chip silent" result was an
  **ordering bug in `--init`**, not hardware: `RequestHwVersion` is ignored
  until the NVRAM exchange has run.
- Verified prologue on `/dev/ttySAC0` 921600 8N1, no flow control, after
  `GPS_PWR_EN` 0 (1 s) -> 1 (0.25 s):
  1. `80` x16 autobaud -> no announce (normal);
  2. `fe00fd001b07000000fc` -> no reply, but stores the word;
  3. `ff00fd001bfc` -> `fe00fd001b 07000000 fc`;
  4. `ff00fd401afc` -> `fe00fd401a 00000000 fc` (`020010a4` on a cold boot);
  5. `ff00fd0000fc` -> `fe00fd0000 05000230 fc` (version `0x30020005`);
  6. `ff00fd1f95fc` -> `fe00fd1f95 00000000 fc` (sub 0x95 = asic-ready ACK).
  `GetOutOfLegacy` is **not** answered here; after step 6 the chip is silent
  for 6 s and polls stay constant — no measurement stream, no NMEA.
- Flow control is irrelevant: `CRTSCTS`, manual RTS, both, and both after a
  power cycle gave zero rx over 10 s x3. 14-baud sweep (4800..4M) after a power
  pulse: zero rx. Pinmux pins 87-90 (gpb0-4..7) -> `13800000.uart`; gpio137
  writes move the pin `out lo`/`out hi`.
- NMEA is produced by `glgps`, never by the chip; the remaining vendor stages
  (flow-control search, ESW upload, RF/clock plan, measurement start) are
  run-time computed and the ROM has no ESW blob.
- Next experiment: one cold-start capture of the stock stack (pad tap or stock
  boot log) and replay; alternatively disassemble
  `Bri_ProgramSwFlowControl` (`0x2a6aa0`) against the ACK parser (`0x2a789c`).
- `j7elte-gpsd --init` must send the NVRAM pair before `RequestHwVersion` and
  must not abort when autobaud is unannounced (GpsToolchain is implementing).

===APKBUILD
# Maintainer: ROM/Nura parity integration (SM-J700M / j7elte)
#
# SIPC5 RIL client for the Shannon SS310AP modem on the Exynos 7580.
#
# Stock Android telephony is rild + libril.so + libsec-ril.so, all bionic and
# not installable on a musl rootfs.  libsec-ril.so speaks a proprietary
# "IpcProtocol" message layer over the kernel's SIPC5 FMT/RFS channels; this
# package is a from-scratch implementation of the subset of that protocol that
# was recovered by disassembling the stock library (see
# parity/reports/ril-re.md for every address):
#
#   * opens /dev/umts_ipc0 and /dev/umts_rfs0 -- which is what makes the
#     kernel answer the CP's PHONE_START with INIT_END (rild_ready(),
#     link_device_shmem.c:261) and lets the baseband become usable,
#   * re-issues IOCTL_MODEM_BOOT_OFF when the kernel still reports OFFLINE
#     (a RIL started after j7elte-cbd), because misc_write() rejects messages
#     with -EPERM until mc->phone_state == STATE_ONLINE,
#   * encodes/decodes the 7-byte struct sipc_fmt_hdr message framing that the
#     stock library uses (len/seq/ack/main/sub/type), including reassembly of
#     messages split over several SIPC5 frames,
#   * implements SMS_DEVICE_READY, the MISC version/time/capacity/serial
#     number requests, SEC pin status and SIM power, NET operator and
#     voice/data registration state, and PWR radio/modem power,
#   * decodes the IMEI/MEID reply and the registration-state reply layout.
#
# Calls, SMS and data/PDP are NOT implemented; the gap and the exact missing
# pieces are documented in the report.  Do not expect telephony to work yet.
pkgname=j7elte-ril
pkgver=0.1
pkgrel=0

RIL: userspace deployed, but CP won't power on — kernel/TZ ABI: exynos_smc(0x82000700, READ_CTRL) returns 8; ss310ap_boot_on aborts. This is a kernel bug candidate: `exynos_set_cp_power_onoff` reading CP power status returns 8 (error) and aborts. The stock bootloader sets CP status; maybe the CP_STATUS register (0x8) means "CP is powered off / in reset"? Error code 8 = ? Maybe `CP_POWER_STATUS_OFF`? The code treats nonzero as error.

This is a hardware bring-up blocker for modem. Fix likely in `drivers/misc/modem_if`/`exynos-modem-ctrl.c`: the smc read returns 8 which may be a valid status meaning "powered off"; the driver should proceed to power on anyway. That's a kernel change — candidate for next slice.

Mark RIL todo pending (blocked on kernel/TZ CP power). Actually deliverable is partial; keep pending with note.

Wait for hall + FM backend, then:
1. Reboot window for GPS golden.
2. Kernel work for modem CP power (needs rebuild; combine with GPU CONFIG_DRM? Careful: separate changes).

Given time, after hall/FM, do the reboot golden test, then spawn a modem-kernel agent.

Wait.

content.text:
“Secure world” = ARM TrustZone on the SoC:

- Normal world (your kernel, EL1) can only ask the secure side via `SMC` instructions.
- Secure world runs the **EL3 monitor + a trusted OS/TA** — on this Samsung device that's **Kinibi/TEE** (`/dev/mobicore` exists, console is stock S-Boot).
- CP power control on Exynos is implemented **inside the TEE**, not in the kernel: the kernel calls `exynos_smc(0x82000700, READ/WRITE_CTRL, …)` and the TEE decides whether to grant it.

What we observed:

| Call | Result |
|---|---|
| `SMC(0x82000700, READ_CTRL)` | raw `8` — not the encoded `(val<<16)|0` the kernel expects |
| `SMC(0x82000700, WRITE_CTRL, CP_PWRON|CP_START)` | `write Fail: 8` — denied |
| `MODEM_ON` after | `-EACCES`, CP status stays 0 |

So the modem's power rail is gated by **trusted firmware policy**, not by anything in Linux. A kernel patch can issue the right call, but it cannot override the TEE's refusal — that needs the correct secure ABI/authorization (e.g. the sequence/handles S-Boot used, or a build of the secure stack that permits it). That's why the modem blocker is classified as kernel/TZ parity, not userspace.
