Modem investigation returned a definitive verdict: **not possible on this unit without the stock TrustZone.**

| Evidence | Finding |
|---|---|
| SMC ABI | `0x82000700` subs 3/4 at 17 sites; encoding `(val<<16)|0` proven by `ubfx #0x11` at `0x17fb8`; WRITE constants `0x8/0x40/0x100/0xA` |
| Runtime | READ → `8`, WRITE `0xA` (CP_PWRON\|CP_START) → `8`; kernel prints `write Fail: 8` |
| MMIO | `CP_CTRL` at PA `0x105C0030` is secure-only (normal-world reads expose only `+0x34/38/40/6C`) |
| TEE | Kinibi t-base-EXYNOS64-V015 with libMcClient/Registry + mcDriverDaemon, but **no modem TA** (`.tlbin`/mcRegistry absent); `libsec-ril` has no TEE path |
| Gates excluded | bootmode/cmdline, sec-boot fuses, sys_rev/ds_det, `CP_RST_N`, SHMEM DT, PMIC (no S2MPU01A) |
| Stock sequence | `MODEM_RESET 0x6f21 → SECURITY_REQ mode2 → XMIT_BOOT → mode0 → MODEM_ON` — already replayed, accepted codes match, still no power |

So the CP’s power switch is guarded by secure firmware that doesn’t authorize a non-Android boot; a Linux-side fix can’t override it. Only the stock Android TZ stack or a bootloader-chain replacement would change that.

All of this is in `docs/reports/modem-tz.md` and the state doc. Remaining live work is device-bound (GPS config reply → NMEA, FM audio/RDS, GPU M1 boot) and still waiting on the **power-cycle + re-plug**.

#!/bin/sh
# Reboot/poweroff for j7elte. busybox reboot(2) does not reset this SoC
# (the kernel's restart handler parks in the bootloader); sysrq 'b' does.
set -eu
sync
echo 1 > /proc/sys/kernel/sysrq
case "${1:-reboot}" in
	poweroff|halt|o) echo o > /proc/sysrq-trigger ;;
	*)               echo b > /proc/sysrq-trigger ;;
esac
EOF

open(p,"w").write(s)
EOF

1. Reduce concurrency: kill some agents, run fewer at a time (e.g., 3-4).
2. Reduce memory pressure: avoid parallel kernel builds (each `make -j2` uses GBs); the integrator builds on external drive; TMPDIR off /tmp.
3. Host /tmp is a 9.7G tmpfs (RAM-backed!) — that's a big OOM contributor. Move build scratch/TMPDIR to disk (/run/media/... external) and clean /tmp artifacts.
4. Disable auto-compaction? Not memory.

# gpu31 IRQ — slot routing, mask/clear completion path, resume re-arm

Date: 2026-11-20. Ticket: `p7580_job_hw_submit` (JS registers written),
IRQ handler (STAT/RAWSTAT clear + fence), IRQ registration/masking,
slot selection. Symptom (Main, int15 silicon): NULL job dispatches on
slot 1 (`run_job seq=0 slot=1 sslot=1 jc=0x2000000`,
`pm_get HELD`, `p7580_job: dispatch slot=1 jc=0x2000000
cfg=0x00083700 as=0 aff=0x3 seq=0`), then no `p7580_job: irq` line,
`panfrost7580-job` IRQ count stays 0 (`panfrost7580-gpu` fired once),
and the fence retires on the 5 s timeout instead of by interrupt.

## 1. Register table (gpu31-jobabi §4/§7 vs what the driver writes)

| Register | Offset | Driver write | Reference | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `JOB_INT_RAWSTAT` | `0x1000` | read in irq-enter + post-start + loop | `[KT]` regmap `:203` raw latch | **added reads** (were missing) |
| `JOB_INT_CLEAR` | `0x1004` | `mask` at init/rearm/recover; per-slot `m` in IRQ | `[KT]` `:204` WO clear; `[V5]` `job_write(JOB_INT_CLEAR, mask)` per slot | match (now also cleared via rearm helper) |
| `JOB_INT_MASK` | `0x1008` | `mask & (js_present \| js_present<<16)` at init/rearm | `[KT]` `:205`; kbase `pm_enable_interrupts` writes `0xFFFFFFFF`; `[V5]` `MK_JS_MASK` union | **kept present-gated** (deliberate: kbase unmasks all 16 slots, this port has 3; unmasked STAT ⊆ RAWSTAT either way) |
| `JOB_INT_STAT` | `0x100C` | read as `status` in IRQ demux | `[KT]` `:206`; `[V5]` handler reads STAT | match |
| `JS_HEAD_NEXT_LO/HI` | `slot+0x40/0x44` | `jc` lo/hi | jobabi §4 `0x1840/0x1844` slot 0 | match |
| `JS_AFFINITY_NEXT_LO/HI` | `slot+0x50/0x54` | full `shader_present` | jobabi §4 | match |
| `JS_CONFIG_NEXT` | `slot+0x58` | `p7580_js_config(as_nr)` = `0x3700\|as` → `0x83700` | jobabi §6: START/END CLEAN_INV + START_MMU(10649) + PRI(8), no FLUSH_REDUCTION/JOBCHAIN/PROTECTED | match (`cfg=0x00083700` trace = `as=0` + `0x83700`) |
| `JS_COMMAND_NEXT` | `slot+0x60` | `START 0x01` after `wmb()` | `[KT]` `JS_COMMAND_START`; `[KB]` GO after cfg | match (**added `wmb()`** — HEAD/AFF/CFG must be visible before START latches on this weakly-ordered SoC) |
| `JS_STATUS` | `slot+0x24` | read in IRQ per-slot + post-start dump | jobabi §7 fault table | match (**added post-start + irq-err naming**) |
| `JS_FLUSH_ID_NEXT` | `slot+0x70` | not programmed | no FLUSH_REDUCTION on T720 | match |
| `JOB_IRQ_THROTTLE` | `0x1014` | untouched (0) | kbase writes throttle cycles per IRQ; 0 = deliver immediately | match (no coalescing) |
| `JOB_IRQ_JS_STATE` | `0x1010` | not read | kbase race-check register (jm_hw.c race comment) | **not ported** (single job per slot here; RAWSTAT tail re-check covers the missed-failure race instead) |

Completion condition (jobabi §4+§7): the dispatched job completes when
the handler observes `JOB_INT_STAT & MK_JS_MASK(slot)` with the DONE
bit set, clears the slot bit(s) via `JOB_INT_CLEAR`, and
`dma_fence_signal()`s the in-flight fence. The 5 s `timedout_job`
exists only for the no-IRQ case. Polarity verified against `[KT]`
regmap `:199-208` + `[V5]` `/tmp/pf52/panfrost_regs.h:191-200`.

INSTR_TYPE_MISMATCH... Hmm.

Think: Midgard fragment job requires the "tiler heap" (JS config bit) and the FBD; but mismatch is instruction type.

Maybe the GPU's JS0 expects fragment jobs to have HEAD pointing to a **job header** whose w0..w3 are command words (fragment job descriptor), and w4 is the header with type. Our dispatch writes JS_HEAD_NEXT = jc and starts. That worked for 60 fragment jobs.

Why would one identical descriptor mismatch? Unless this job's bytes at GPU view differ from CPU view *at execution time* (not at dump time). We dump after fault; by then Mesa may have overwritten the BO (the batch was submitted, then panfrost writes new content). Since we don't fence properly? But excl fence added.

Actually the sequence: panfrost builds batch in a BO, submits, then **reuses the same BO for the next batch** (recycling) while GPU still reading. Our submit returns before GPU completes (async queue!), and Mesa's batch submit waits via syncobj? Panfrost waits on the out fence in its own way... but if our sched queue runs jobs later, Mesa may already reuse.

The excl-fence change was supposed to serialize via resv, but Mesa's own buffer management trusts in-fence/out-fence syncobj: panfrost_batch_submit takes a fence and waits? Not necessarily each frame.

The fault on the LAST submit (frame end) suggests the BO for the frame's fragment job gets reused by the *next* frame's tiler build while GPU still executes → torn.

Our driver's out_sync install happens in run_job (async), so the returned syncobj fence is only populated when the job starts; Mesa may query it earlier and see empty → proceeds to reuse BOs.

Fix: install the fence at SUBMIT (sched_job fence from drm_sched_job_arm is available) rather than in run_job. Earlier int13 showed SUBMIT-time fence was NULL at that point (per probe) — but drm_sched_job_arm should create it. In our shim, job->fence is assigned in pump. Proper fix: create the out fence in the shim at submit time (entity->fence) like mainline drm_sched_job_arm does, and return it via syncobj at SUBMIT. That's the real semantic.

So: shim must create a dma_fence at arm time, assign to sched_job->fence, and run_job's completion signals *that* fence (not a new one).

That's a notable change but correct.

Assign G31_ArmFence: implement arm-time fence in the shim and install it on out_sync at SUBMIT; run_job signals it on completion (via scheduling's finish).

# Panfrost on j7elte — final report (2026-11-21)

## What works (verified on silicon, kernel #37 int25)
- **Render-only DRM node**: `/dev/dri/renderD128` only; no `card0`; Xorg/fbdev untouched.
- **Full v5.2 ioctl surface** through our kernel: GET_PARAM (`0x720`), CREATE_BO (shmem-backed,
  16 MiB OK), MMAP_BO, GET_BO_OFFSET, SUBMIT, WAIT_BO, plus generic DRM syncobj (7 ioctls).
- **Job dispatch and completion**: JS0/JS1 routing per mainline (req0 chain -> JS1, FS -> JS0),
  `JS_CONFIG` per jobabi, IRQ demux (STAT|RAWSTAT), fence signal on IRQ, bounded timeouts,
  PM lifetime + teardown guards, clean close.
- **GPU memory writes**: Zero-fill WRITE_VALUE over a page pre-filled `0xA5A5A5A5` -> both
  kernel (`DEBUG_READ_BO`) and user views read 0. Coherency model (dma_map bind,
  sync_for_device submit, pre-signal sync_for_cpu) verified.
- **Mesa 20.3.5 drives the GPU**: `GL vendor=Panfrost`, `renderer=Mali T720 (Panfrost)`,
  GLES 3.0; hundreds of submits per run; **framebuffer clear is pixel-exact**
  (`RGBA=26,26,102,255`).

## The one open defect
Per frame, exactly one submit faults:
```
p7580_job: ERR slot=0 js_status=0x00000052 (INSTR_TYPE_MISMATCH)
    head=tail=0x21c5600 jc=0x21c5600 seq=121 w4=0x00010013 w5=0 cfg=0x00083700
p7580_job: ERR-MAP ... h6=0x21c5000/0x10000 ... (no overlapping live mappings)
```
- Descriptor bytes are legal (64-bit header, type 9 FRAGMENT), byte-identical in shape to
  fragment jobs that complete.
- Deterministic: same slot, same type, always the last submit of Mesa's flush batch; code
  varies slightly (0x52/0x58) with freed-page contents.
- Fixes tried and verified as *not* the cause: slot routing, JOBCHAIN bit, excl-fence publish,
  IOVA overlap (0 overlaps), arm-time fence install.
- Leading hypothesis after all measurements: the GPU's view of the instruction buffer differs
  from the kernel's view at execution time (BO reuse / PTE-TLB lifetime across Mesa's batch
  pool), i.e. a *visibility/timing* defect, not an encoding one.

## Next experiment (single, decisive)
Instrument the **PTE path at fault time**: on ERR, walk the AS0 page tables for `jc` and compare
the leaf's physical page against the owning BO's current page array, then also re-read that
physical page via `kmap` in the same handler. If they differ, it is a page-table/IOVA lifetime
bug (fix in map/unmap + invalidate ordering); if they match, the GPU's fetch is stale only in
its own cache/TLB and needs a stronger invalidate before `START`.

## Delivered patches (repo)
- `patches/drm-backport/0001-0005` (fence/resv/syncobj/sched shims, 280 host checks)
- `code/gpu31/kms` Mode-B v2 render-only
- `code/gpu31/{gem,jobs,mmu,iommu,power,devfreq,dmabuf}` + driver 0001/0002
- Reports: `gpu31-*.md` (target, iommu, mmu, jobs, gem, dmabuf, kms, drmcore, sched, pm-order,
  close-fix, submit-hw, jobtrace, probernumeric, opsfix, abialign, gpuwrite, coherency,
  mesa-render, tilerchain, primitive, errtrace, instrtype, iova, armfence, integrations 1-25)

## Status summary
| Area | State |
|---|---|
| Kernel driver | complete and stable (render-only, PM, close, syncobj, shmem) |
| GPU execution | works (jobs, IRQ, fences, memory writes) |
| Mesa bring-up | works (renderer, submits, clear) |
| Draw geometry | **open**: one deterministic fragment fault per frame |
| 2D / UI | unaffected, fbdev X healthy |

The walker call is AFTER the dark early-return: if `p7580_drv_pm_get(drv)` returns non-zero (dark), it signals and returns **before** ptewalk. Our PM get apparently returns nonzero in the timeout path → no walk.

Wait: pm_get returns 0 or 1 (success), negative error. Code `if (p7580_drv_pm_get(drv))` treats 1 (already active) as failure! That's a bug: pm_runtime_get_sync returns 1 when already active.

So on timeout, get_sync returns 1 (device active since job holds ref) → treated as "dark" → early return with fence signal, skipping recover AND ptewalk.

That also means **timeout recovery never runs**! And the ERR path is IRQ (separate).

Fix: treat >=0 as success (per earlier comment "may return 1 (already active) or 0... Only negative means dark").

So in timedout_job, the check should be `< 0`. This explains no PTEWALK and no recover.

Also similar misuse may exist elsewhere (pm_get helper already handles: p7580_drv_pm_get returns 0/negative? It returns ret from pm_runtime_get_sync, so 1 possible). Callers using `if (pm_get)` are buggy.

This is a real bug: recover skipped.

Fix: helper should normalize (return 0 on success, negative on error). Check p7580_drv_pm_get implementation: earlier comment said "may return 1 (already active) or 0 (resumed now): both mean powered. Only a negative errno means dark." So callers must check <0. The timedout uses `if (p7580_drv_pm_get(drv))` → wrong.

Patch: change to `< 0`, and audit all call sites.

Assign to a quick fix slice, then rebuild int27 and rerun — this may also fix the fault (recover path) but more importantly enables PTEWALK.

content.text: Found a real bug in the diagnosis path: `pm_runtime_get_sync()` returns **1** when the device is already active, but `p7580_drv_timedout_job()` treats any non-zero as “dark” and **early-returns** — so neither timeout recovery nor the PTEWALK probe ever runs. All `pm_get` call sites need `>= 0` (only negative means dark).

For a fragment job on JS0, the job body starts with the FBD, then shader state commands, then FRAGMENT job command. If the body contains a TILER job command (0x0?) → mismatch.

Given depth and time: it's likely a shader (FS) descriptor issue — Mesa's fragment job jumps to a shader descriptor; if our memory contains unrelocated pointers (shader index), the GPU may read garbage → mismatch.

Fix: use VM_MIXEDMAP + vm_insert_page + get_page/put_page to hold refs.

We pin pages with get_page at create (we do single-ref pin) — but vm_insert_page requires refs too.

Anyway: implement VM_MIXEDMAP fault + refs.

content.text: Root cause of the zeroed shader: the BO’s page is **wiped after Mesa writes it** (a `clear_highpage`-class event during the next BO create/map), because our mmap uses `remap_pfn_range`/`VM_PFNMAP` and holds **no page reference** for the mapping. Rewriting the ISA at every submit removes the fault entirely — so the data, not the code, is being freed underneath.

content.thinking:
Precise cause: tiler consumes PRE-VS content; VS→tiler not visible within one chained submit on this hardware (needs a submit boundary with END clean + in_sync).

Solution: split chain into two submits: VS submit (with END_FLUSH_CLEAN_INV) then TILER submit depending on it. But their experiment (split) faulted JS1 POWER_FAULT — because their split implementation was from the hook (user-space) and duplicated chains incorrectly.

Proper fix in the kernel driver: when a submit's chain contains VERTEX then TILER, split it into two submits (kernel-side), or set END_FLUSH on the vertex job.

Actually Midgard hardware requires a "cache flush" between? kbase submits VS and tiler as separate atoms in a chain? In kbase, each "job" in a chain is separate but the chain includes CACHE_FLUSH job? Kbase's job chain supports only one job per slot; VS and tiler are separate atoms submitted sequentially by userspace (panfrost does 3 ioctls?) Hmm, Mesa submits chain as one ioctl with a list of jobs; the kernel (panfrost 5.2) also submits them as one chain with deps!

But our hardware shows the handoff doesn't work within a chain. Maybe because our chain executes but the VS's writes need "END_FLUSH_CLEAN_INV" on the vertex job itself — panfrost sets JS_CONFIG end-flush per job? Our cfg applies END_FLUSH_CLEAN_INV (bits 12-13) to the *whole* submit, which should flush at end of the chain only.

Per-job cfg isn't a thing (one cfg per submit), so chain-level flush happens at chain end — after tiler already ran. Hence tiler sees stale.

Mainline solution: kbase splits VS and tiler into separate submits? In kbase, atoms are grouped: a "job chain" runs multiple jobs but each job slot is separate; kbase submits vertex/tiler/fragment as separate atoms with dependencies, each with its own JS_CONFIG END flush.

So the correct fix: split the chain into separate submits per job, with dependency, so each gets a flush boundary.

Why did their split fault POWER_FAULT? Because splitting requires the *next* job's header to not be linked (next pointer) and proper deps; their duplicate approach likely re-ran chains.

Implement kernel-side split: in submit, parse the chain (job headers have next pointers) and submit each job as its own sched job with dependency on the previous, sequencing to the same slot? But panfrost UAPI expects one jc per submit; the kernel's drm_sched would run them sequentially on the entity.

Simplest robust approach: driver splits a chained submit into N scheduled sub-jobs (walk next pointers), each with END_FLUSH_CLEAN_INV, deps chained, same slot; the ioctl returns after queueing; completion fence signalled by the last.

That's a significant change but well-defined.

Given the user's persistence, spawn G31_ChainSplit to implement this in the driver, with careful handling (next pointers, jc offsets, refs), build int37, flash, test.

Also Defect B remains (FS ISA zero) — with bins present, FS invoked and faults; needs fixing too. Their REUPLOAD masks it; maybe after split, B still hits.

But B's cause: ISA page intermittently zero despite refs. With mapping refs, why zero? Possibly the BO page is freed by Mesa (GEM close) while a submit still references it? We ref BOs in job->bos (now stamped), so pages held... unless ref taken on wrong object.

Let's focus A (split), then B.

Spawn ChainSplit.

content.text:
Now the mechanism is nailed: within one chained submit the **tiler consumes the pre-VS content** of the position buffer — the VS stores only become visible at the submit’s END flush, which happens after the tiler already ran. Enabling the chain bit doesn’t help.

So the fix is a **submit boundary between VS and tiler** (each with its own flush), done in the driver rather than from userspace.

arguments.context:
# Proven on silicon (int36, docs/reports/gpu31-chainexec.md)
- Mesa submits ONE chain per batch: `WRITE_VALUE(idx2,w4=0x00020005) -> VERTEX(idx1,0x0001000b) -> TILER(idx3,0x0003000f)`, next=NULL terminated; tiler deps on the earlier jobs.
- Control probe: at tiler completion the position buffer already holds the VS triangle, yet **tiles_nonempty=0**.
- Prefill probe: a CPU triangle written into Draw.Position **before** submit is consumed by the tiler (bins exactly tile 0), and the VS provably overwrites it later.
- Conclusion: the tiler reads the PRE-VS content; the VS→tiler handoff is not visible inside one chained submit. Setting JS_CONFIG bit 11 does not change it; JS_CONFIG flushes are per-submit.
- Userspace chain splitting/duplication is not viable (POWER_FAULT, poisoning both slots, watchdog resets).
- Defect B (FS ISA page intermittently all-zero) remains; with bins present the fragment invokes the FS and stalls on 0x52.

Required: kernel-side split of the chain at the VS/TILER boundary (or per job), each submit with END_FLUSH_CLEAN_INV, dependencies chained, same slot semantics, completion fence from the last job; the ioctl must still return a single out_sync covering the whole split.

Files: driver 0001 submit.c (chain walk, sched queueing), code/gpu31/jobs (jm_hw cfg), patches/drm-backport/0004 (deps), docs/reports/gpu31-{chainexec,jobabi,multidep,serialfence}.md.

Repo /tmp/j7repo; patches only; commit own files; external disk only; no flash (Main). Phone on int36; /data tooling; plain runs only (no sync/trace).

tasks.solutionSpace: Kernel-side chain splitting with per-job flush and dependency; must preserve one out_sync and slot semantics.

# Target
Chained submit handling in the driver.

Walk the submitted chain (`next` pointers), enqueue each job as its own scheduled run with END_FLUSH_CLEAN_INV and a dependency on the previous, all on the correct slot; install the ioctl's out_sync on the FINAL job's fence (or a join fence); keep bo list refs and PM lifetime per job. Add host tests for ordering, single out-fence, and error unwinding. Hand to integrator; silicon acceptance = PC2_POLLSCAN control shows the VS triangle's tile set (non-empty, not exactly 1) and pixels advance (red once Defect B is fixed).

# Acceptance
docs/reports/gpu31-chainsplit.md with the design, host tests, and the exact silicon verification. Commit + hand to integrator.

arguments.context:
# Defect B (int36, docs/reports/gpu31-polycensus2.md, gpu31-shaderbo.md, gpu31-mmaprefs.md)
The fragment-shader ISA page (e.g. 0x21d6000, 4 KiB SHMEM BO, GEM handle 8) intermittently reads **all-zero** through `DEBUG_READ_BO` (0xCF) at submit time, even though the ledger shows `count=4 mapcount=1 vma=1 pin=1 up lru swapb clean mapping=0 pgidx=0` with the page reference fix in place. Rewriting the ISA before submit (PAN_FBD_REUPLOAD) removes the fault — so the GPU is reading the page and it is genuinely zero.

Established eliminations: wrong BO/address, never written, tag/meta packing, cache direction, swap/migration, BO close/eviction, VMA mismatch, partial write loss; page refs now held.

Files: code/gpu31/gem (shmem page array, free path, ledger), driver 0001, client 0xCF read; docs/reports/gpu31-{shaderbo,mmaprefs,cachedir,fbdtarget}.md. Phone on int36; /data tooling; plain runs only.

Repo /tmp/j7repo; patches only; commit own files; external disk only; no flash (Main).

content.text:
Defect B is solved analytically and fixed in code: `shmem_getpage_gfp()` leaves a **dirty zero line** in the kernel’s linear alias (this arm64 tree’s `flush_dcache_page()` only clears `PG_dcache_clean`), and because the BO VMA is write-combining, the CPU’s ISA stores go straight to DRAM while that stale line later evicts over them — whole page zeroed 0–5 ms after the write. A 2 s pre-sleep before the write prevents it; 31/32 trials reproduce it without any GPU.

Fix: `__flush_dcache_area(page, PAGE_SIZE)` right after each `shmem_read_mapping_page()`. Building int38 for that.

## SUCCESS 2026-11-22 — hardware 3D renders on j7elte
Kernel **int38** (`42d3a160…`, kernel `3bbcc91a…`) on silicon:

- `pf7580-selftest --defectb-test` → **PASS 32/32**, `lost-immediate=0`, `lost-after-3000us=0`
  (the shmem linear-alias dirty-line defect is fixed by `__flush_dcache_area()`).
- `egltest --offscreen-only` (Mesa 20.3.5, `MESA_LOADER_DRIVER_OVERRIDE=panfrost`) →
  `GL vendor='Panfrost'`, `renderer='Mali T720 (Panfrost)'`, GLES 3.0,
  corner `RGBA=26,26,102,255` (clear), centre `RGBA=255,0,0,255` (triangle),
  **`RENDER_OK` / `PASS`**, three consecutive runs, `ERRCOUNT=0` GPU faults.
- Throughput in that test: 60 draws at 256x256 in ~0.17 s (~350 FPS incl. readback).

Winning fixes that made it work (all in this tree):
1. render-only DRM node (no `card0`), full v5.2 ioctls + syncobj, PM lifetime/teardown guards.
2. job submission: slot routing, IRQ STAT|RAWSTAT demux, arm-time fence + syncobj semantics,
   multi-in-fence dependencies, per-file serialisation.
3. GEM: shmem-backed BOs, `VM_MIXEDMAP` page references, correct cache directions, and the
   `__flush_dcache_area()` fix for the shmem zero-line inheriting over WC stores.
4. driver-side chain split with correct 192-byte VERTEX/TILER payloads, giving the
   VS→tiler submit boundary (flush) that Midgard needs.
5. Mesa 20.3.5 paired with the v5.2 UAPI; attribute-array bounds fix (0007).

Known follow-ups: glmark2 cannot run surfaceless on this stack (canvas only), so benchmark
numbers must come from our own EGL clients; debug probes (`0xCF`, JDBODY/PTEWALK/ledger,
`chain_mode`) are marked for strip before cutover.
EOF
git add docs/reports/gpu31-final.md && git commit -qm "docs: SUCCESS - hardware 3D renders on int38 (RENDER_OK, centre red, 0 errors, 3/3 runs)" && git log --oneline -1

content.text:
Numbers, measured on the phone (same client, same shader, 256×256, readback per frame):

| Engine | Frames | Time | FPS |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Panfrost (Mali T720)** via `egltest` | 60 draws | 0.168 s | **≈357** |
| **llvmpipe (software)** same client | 30 | 0.105 s | **≈472** (and ≈284 at 512²) |

So, honestly: **in this microbenchmark the GPU is not yet faster** — it’s ~25% slower at 256², and at 512² it currently **fails** (52 `TIMEOUT` events; rendering there needs Mesa’s multi-FBD path we don’t support yet).

Why the GPU isn’t winning here:
- The scene is trivial: 3 vertices, 65k pixels — dominated by per-submit overhead (ioctl → sched → chain split → IRQ → fence), not by shading.
- Every frame does a full **readback** (`glReadPixels`), which on our stack costs a sync + cache maintenance; llvmpipe has the pixels in CPU cache already.
- No zero-copy presentation path (panfrost has no KMS/DRM display node; we blit via fb0), so the demo path adds a copy.
- The T720 MP2 at 266–668 MHz is a small GPU; llvmpipe on 8 A53 cores is genuinely competitive for tiny workloads.

Where the GPU should win is fill-heavy, many-frame work — which needs the 512²/MFBD fix and ideally a benchmark that doesn’t read back every frame. That’s the next engineering step if you want a “faster than software” result rather than just correct rendering.

The on-screen demo itself did run purely on the GPU (`GL_RENDERER: Mali T720 (Panfrost)`, 20 fps animated triangle blitted to fb0).

1. **Fault fences are slow, not wrong:** on a fault the ERR path doesn’t signal; the 5 s scheduler timeout does. Fix in flight — kick `timeout_work` at delay 0 from the fault IRQ.
2. **Readback race:** `SUBMIT` returns before the out-fence is published on the BO reservation, so a `WAIT_BO`/`glReadPixels` in that window can read before the job completes. Also confirmed: T720 is **SFBD-only**, so 512² is one FBD; the 4 MiB polygon list is just an 8-px-vs-16-px tile-size over-allocation in Mesa, harmless.

**Fix:** publish only at SUBMIT, inside `serial_lock` (publish order == submit order); no UAPI or recovery change.

Two things from my side for the leak hunt, free to use or ignore:
1. The extra work my patch adds per fragment submit is one `p7580_drv_gpu_read(walk + 40, 4)` — it takes exactly one GEM ref in `p7580_drv_gpu_span()` and drops it on every path in `p7580_drv_gpu_read()`, so it cannot account for pages. `fbd`/`jc_age` are plain u32 fields and the age ledger is a 64-entry array inside `p7580_drv_file` (no allocation). If the leak rate changes at all between int44 and int45 that is worth checking first.
2. In every storm capture the per-frame BO set is *identical*: same 10 handles, same IOVAs, same 64 KiB slab (`h6`) every frame, so the growth is per-page references on reused BOs, not new BOs — consistent with your gem_names finding. Given ~10 BOs/frame and 1.16 MB/frame, the plausible shape is one missing `put_page` per mapped page per submit (mmap pin/unpin or the free-path ref walk), i.e. the same pages get an extra ref each frame while the BOs are reused.

Wall time: 2.06 seconds

The leak is closed and pushed (`44d3c26`).

**int45 silicon**
| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `map == unmap` (iova trace) | **19 : 19** (was 19 : 3) |
| Shmem per 300-frame run | **+24 / +104 / +104 kB** (was ~1.2 MB per frame) |
| ERR / TIMEOUT / WARN | 0 / 0 / 0 across 3 runs |
| Post-exit growth | none (`gem_names` empty) |
| 512² readback | clean, 42–49 fps |

Root cause: `bo_list` held a `drm_gem_object_reference` whose only drop lived in `gem_free_object` — the reference made its own release unreachable, so every submitted BO pinned its private shmem inode, pages and IOVA forever. Fixed by making the entry weak + `kref_get_unless_zero` resurrection only under `bo_lock`, with bind rollback.

Two follow-ups are now in `G31_MMLock`:
1. **Crash**: unlocked `drm_gem_create_mmap_offset`/`free` race `drm_gem_mmap`’s `offset_hash` → `LIST_POISON2` oops in `drm_mm_insert_helper`. Needs a driver-private lock (struct_mutex is unavailable in `free_object`), stress-proven.
2. **fps 101 vs 155**: the formerly-skipped per-frame teardown (288 PTE clears, 3 TLB invalidates, 288 `dma_unmap_page`/`put_page`) needs batching/deferral, measured piece by piece.

Residual open defect, now precisely defined: a **silent `js_status 0x08` timeout, ~1 per 4–6 runs**, costing 750 ms + recovery; worst reproducer is 512² pre-finish readback. int48 (diagnostic overlay: per-class timers behind `prof_arm`, plus independent `submit_err` attribution) is building so a failing run names the error path instead of swallowing it.

arguments.content:
int48 runtime defect, diagnosed from the flashed image: `p7580/prof_arm` does not exist. `p7580_prof_debugfs_init()` calls `debugfs_create_dir("p7580", NULL)`; that directory is already created by the driver, so the call returns `-EEXIST`, `IS_ERR_OR_NULL` is false (it's an ERR_PTR), and the function returns before creating `prof_arm`. My runs printed `can't create /sys/kernel/debug/p7580/prof_arm: Permission denied` and `ls` confirms only chain_mode/dump/ev_arm/hang_inject/iova_arm/job_timeout_ms/serialize_fs/trace_arm.

Fix in the overlay (int49): reuse the existing root dir — `debugfs_lookup("p7580", NULL)` (or keep a drv field for the dir created by the driver) and create `prof_arm` inside it; on `-EEXIST`-class failure log at `p7580perf:` level, never return silently. Also add a probe-time sanity check so this cannot regress unseen.

Separately for the record, from the flashed int48 (unarmed): 4×300 = 158.8 / 105.8 / 155.5 / 151.4 fps, 0 aborts, 0 ERR/TO; 4×512²×40 readback = 60.6 / 54.9 / 38.3 / 39.8 fps, all clean (no timeouts) — so the 0x08 storm did not reproduce in that window.

## GPU stable at 155 fps; leak, race, and fps regression fixed (2026-11-22, int47/int48)
Kernel **int48** (Image 911e7bf1..., boot 70345435...; driver 0001 04db08d, overlay 952ff750...).
- BO/shmem leak: `bo_list` held a strong GEM ref whose only drop lived in `gem_free_object`,
  so every submitted BO pinned its shmem inode for ever (~1.16 MB/frame). Entry is now weak,
  resurrection only via `kref_get_unless_zero` under `bo_lock`; Shmem flat at 2-3 MB across runs.
- mmap-offset race: driver-owned offset manager + one leaf lock; `.mmap` no longer calls
  `drm_gem_mmap`; 1000-iteration churn clean (client bug in the test fixed separately).
- fps 101 -> 155: the 3.10 `dma_fence_wait_timeout` shim returned the bare budget for a
  *signaled* fence, so a 0-jiffy poll looked like "budget exhausted" and `WAIT_BO` (correctly)
  said ETIMEDOUT; Mesa's BO cache never hit (794 WAIT_BO/frame, 4.1 CREATE_BO/frame).
  After the shim fix: 4.3 WAIT_BO/frame, 1.0 CREATE_BO/frame, client sys 5.4 -> 1.7 ms/frame.
- Silicon (locked, uncontended): 300 f at 256^2 = 155.7/155.0/157.4/154.4/158.1 fps, 0 ERR/TO;
  512^2 30-40 f readback clean; 8x512^2x40 readback loop clean.
- Residual: silent `js_status 0x08` timeout ~1 per 4-6 runs (750 ms + recovery). int48's
  diagnostic overlay should name it, but `p7580/prof_arm` fails to register
  (`debugfs_create_dir("p7580")` returns -EEXIST); int49 fixes that. `submit_err` now logs
  `n=` and is independent of the 8-line sched_trace budget.
'''
open(p,'w').write(s.rstrip()+'\n'+add)
